title.zh: 卷218 列傳五 诸王四 太祖诸子三
title.en: Volume 218 Biographies 5: Princes 4: Tai Zu Zhu Zi San
title.raw: 卷218 列傳五 诸王四 太祖诸子三

sentences.zh: 睿忠親王多爾袞，太祖第十四子。

translations.literal: Prince Rui the Loyal and Faithful, Dorgon, was the fourteenth son of the Taizu [Nurhaci].
translations.idiomatic: Dorgon, Prince Rui the Loyal and Faithful, was the fourteenth son of Taizu.

sentences.zh: 初封貝勒。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as a beile.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created a beile.

sentences.zh: 天聰二年，太宗伐察哈爾多羅特部，破敵於敖穆楞，多爾袞有功，賜號墨爾根代青。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancong, the Taizong attacked the Dorot tribe of the Chakhar; he defeated the enemy at Aomuleng. Dorgon had merit and was granted the title Mo'ergen Daiqing.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 2 (1628), Hong Taiji campaigned against the Chakhar Dorot; after the victory at Aomuleng, Dorgon was rewarded with the honorific Mo'ergen Daiqing for his service.

sentences.zh: 三年，從上自龍井關入明邊，與貝勒莽古爾泰等攻下漢兒莊，趨通州，薄明都，敗袁崇煥、祖大壽援兵於廣渠門外，又殲山海關援兵於薊州。

translations.literal: In the third year, he followed the sovereign in entering Ming territory through Longjing Pass; together with Beile Manggu'ertai and others he took Han'erzhuang, advanced toward Tongzhou, and pressed close to the Ming capital. He defeated the relief forces of Yuan Chonghuan and Zu Dashou outside the Guangqu Gate, and annihilated the Shanhaiguan relief army at Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he followed the khan through Longjing Pass into Ming territory. With Manggu'ertai and others he captured Han'erzhuang, marched on Tongzhou, and threatened Beijing, routing Yuan Chonghuan's and Zu Dashou's relief troops at Guangqu Gate and destroying the Shanhaiguan column at Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，引還，多爾袞與莽古爾泰先行，复破敵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year [the army] withdrew; Dorgon and Manggu'ertai went ahead and again defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew in the fourth year, Dorgon and Manggu'ertai led the van and routed the enemy again.

sentences.zh: 五年，初設六部，掌吏部事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the Six Ministries were first established, [he] took charge of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, with the founding of the Six Ministries, he was put in charge of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 從上圍大凌河，戰，多爾袞陷陣，明兵墮壕者百餘，城上砲矢發，將士有死者。

translations.literal: Following the sovereign in besieging Daling River, in battle Dorgon plunged into the enemy ranks; more than a hundred Ming soldiers fell into the moat, cannon and arrows were fired from the walls, and some officers and soldiers were killed.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Daling River, Dorgon charged deep into the enemy lines. Over a hundred Ming troops tumbled into the moat under a hail of cannon fire and arrows from the walls, and several of his own officers and men were killed.

sentences.zh: 上切責諸將不之阻。

translations.literal: The sovereign sharply rebuked the generals for not stopping him.
translations.idiomatic: The khan sternly rebuked the generals for failing to hold him back.

sentences.zh: 祖大壽約以錦州獻，多爾袞與阿巴泰等以兵四千，僑裝從大壽作潰奔狀，襲錦州，錦州兵迎戰，擊敗之。

translations.literal: When Zu Dashou agreed to surrender Jinzhou, Dorgon with Abatai and others took four thousand troops, disguised themselves, and following Zu Dashou in feigned rout, raided Jinzhou; the Jinzhou troops came out to fight and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: After Zu Dashou pledged to hand over Jinzhou, Dorgon and Abatai led four thousand men in disguise, feigning flight with Zu Dashou's column to strike Jinzhou. The garrison sallied forth and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 事具阿巴泰傳。

translations.literal: The affair is fully recorded in Abatai's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Abatai's biography.

sentences.zh: 六年五月，從征察哈爾。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixth year, he joined the campaign against the Chakhar.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixth year he took part in the expedition against the Chakhar.

sentences.zh: 七年六月，詔問徵明及朝鮮、察哈爾三者何先，多爾袞言：「宜整兵馬，乘穀熟時，入邊圍燕京，截其援兵，毀其屯堡，為久駐計，可坐待其敝。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year, an edict asked which of attacking Ming, Korea, or the Chakhar should come first; Dorgon said: "We should ready troops and horses, and when the grain is ripe enter the borderlands, besiege Yanjing, cut off relief forces, destroy fortified settlements, and plan for a prolonged stay—we can wait for them to wear themselves out.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventh year the court asked whether Ming, Korea, or the Chakhar should be struck first. Dorgon replied: "Mass the army and wait until the harvest is in, then cross the border, invest Yanjing, sever their relief columns, and raze their outposts. Settle in for a long siege and let exhaustion do the rest.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，從上伐明，克保安，略朔州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year, he followed the sovereign in campaigning against Ming, captured Bao'an, and raided Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year he marched against Ming with the khan, took Bao'an, and swept through Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 九年，上命偕岳託等將萬人招察哈爾林丹汗子額哲，師還，渡河，多爾袞自平魯衛至朔州，毀寧武關，略代州、忻州、崞縣、黑峰口及應州，復自歸化攜降眾還。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the sovereign ordered him to join Yueto and others in leading ten thousand men to summon Esen, son of Ligdan Khan of the Chakhar; when the army returned after crossing the river, Dorgon went from Pingluwei to Shuozhou, destroyed Ningwu Pass, raided Daizhou, Xizhou, Guoxian, Heifengkou, and Yingzhou, then returned from Guihua with the surrendered populace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was sent with Yueto and others at the head of ten thousand men to receive Esen, Ligdan Khan's Chakhar heir. On the return march, after crossing the river, Dorgon struck from Pingluwei to Shuozhou, broke Ningwu Pass, and raided Daizhou, Xizhou, Guoxian, Heifengkou, and Yingzhou before coming back through Guihua with the surrendered peoples.

sentences.zh: 林丹汗得元玉璽曰「制誥之寶」，多爾袞使額哲進上，羣臣因表上尊號。

translations.literal: Ligdan Khan obtained the Yuan jade seal called "Seal for Issuing Edicts and Decrees"; Dorgon had Esen present it to the sovereign, whereupon the officials submitted a memorial requesting an honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: Ligdan Khan had come into possession of the Yuan imperial seal known as "The Seal for Edicts and Commands." Dorgon had Esen present it to the throne, and the ministers thereupon memorialized for a new imperial title.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，進封睿親王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, he was advanced to Prince Rui.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongde 1 he was promoted to Prince Rui.

sentences.zh: 武英郡王阿濟格等率師伐明，命王偕多鐸攻山海關綴明師，阿濟格捷至，乃還。

translations.literal: Prince Wuying Ajige and others led troops against Ming; the Prince was ordered to join Dodo in attacking Shanhaiguan to pin down Ming forces; when Ajige arrived with victory, they returned.
translations.idiomatic: While Prince Wuying Ajige led a column against Ming, the Prince was ordered to join Dodo at Shanhaiguan to tie down Ming reinforcements. Once Ajige reported success, both forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 從伐朝鮮，偕豪格別從寬甸入長山口，克昌州。

translations.literal: He joined the campaign against Korea; with Hooge he separately entered through Kuandian via Changshankou and captured Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Korean campaign he and Hooge took a separate route through Kuandian and Changshankou and seized Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 進攻江華島，克之，獲朝鮮王妃及其二子，國王李倧請降。

translations.literal: He advanced against Ganghwa Island, captured it, took the Korean queen and her two sons, and King Yi Jong requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He assaulted Ganghwa Island, took it, and captured the Korean queen and her two sons, after which King Yi Jong sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 上還盛京，命約束後軍，攜朝鮮質子鷫、淏及大臣子以歸。

translations.literal: The sovereign returned to Shengjing and ordered [him] to keep the rear forces in order and bring back the Korean hostages Su and Ho and the sons of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When the khan returned to Shengjing, he was charged with marshaling the rear guard and escorting home the Korean hostages Su and Ho along with the sons of court ministers.

sentences.zh: 三年，上伐喀爾喀，王留守，築遼陽都爾弼城，城成，命曰屏城；

translations.literal: In the third year, when the sovereign campaigned against the Khalkha, the Prince remained on garrison duty and built the city of Du'erbi at Liaoyang; when it was completed it was named Pingcheng ("Screen City");
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, while the khan campaigned against the Khalkha, the Prince stayed behind to garrison the realm. He built a fortress at Du'erbi in Liaoyang and, when it was finished, named it Pingcheng—the Screen City;

sentences.zh: 復治盛京至遼河大道。

translations.literal: he also repaired the great road from Shengjing to the Liao River.
translations.idiomatic: he also rebuilt the main highway from Shengjing to the Liao River.

sentences.zh: 八月，命為奉命大將軍，將左翼，岳託將右翼，伐明。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, he was appointed Grand General by Imperial Command, commanding the Left Wing while Yueto commanded the Right Wing, to attack Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he received the seal of Grand General by Imperial Command, leading the Left Wing while Yueto led the Right, and marched against Ming.

sentences.zh: 自董家口毀邊牆入，約右翼兵會通州河西務。

translations.literal: They entered by breaking through the border wall at Dongjiakou and arranged to meet the Right Wing at Hexiwu, west of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They breached the frontier wall at Dongjiakou and set a rendezvous with the right wing at Hexiwu, west of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 越明都至涿州，分兵八道，行略地至山西，南徇保定，擊破明總督盧像升。

translations.literal: Passing the Ming capital they reached Zhuozhou, divided into eight columns, raided as far as Shanxi, swept south toward Baoding, and defeated Ming Grand Secretary Lu Xiangsheng.
translations.idiomatic: They skirted Beijing for Zhuozhou, split into eight columns, and plundered deep into Shanxi before turning south on Baoding, where they shattered the Ming Grand Secretary Lu Xiangsheng.

sentences.zh: 遂趨臨清，渡運河，破濟南。

translations.literal: They then pressed toward Linqing, crossed the Grand Canal, and stormed Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: The army then drove on Linqing, crossed the Grand Canal, and broke Jinan.

sentences.zh: 還略天津、遷安，出青山關。

translations.literal: On the return march they raided Tianjin and Qian'an and exited through Qingshan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On the way back they harried Tianjin and Qian'an and withdrew through Qingshan Pass.

sentences.zh: 克四十餘城，降六城，俘戶口二十五萬有奇，賜馬五、銀二萬。

translations.literal: They captured more than forty cities, received the surrender of six, took over two hundred fifty thousand-odd households, and were rewarded with five horses and twenty thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign yielded more than forty captured cities, six surrenders, and over a quarter-million people seized; the Prince was granted five horses and twenty thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 五年，屯田義州，克錦州城西九台，刈其禾。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, [he] garrisoned and farmed at Yizhou, captured the nine forts west of Jinzhou city, and reaped their grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he established garrison farms at Yizhou, took the nine redoubts west of Jinzhou, and harvested their fields.

sentences.zh: 又克小凌河西二台。

translations.literal: He also captured the two forts west of the Xiao Ling River.
translations.idiomatic: He also seized the two forts west of the Xiao Ling River.

sentences.zh: 迭敗明兵杏山、松山間。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated Ming forces between Xingshan and Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he beat Ming troops in the ground between Xingshan and Songshan.

sentences.zh: 圍錦州，王貝勒移營去城三十里，又令每旗一將校率每牛錄甲士五人先歸。

translations.literal: When besieging Jinzhou, the Prince and the beiles moved camp thirty li from the city and also ordered one officer from each banner to lead five armored soldiers from each niru to return first.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Jinzhou the Prince and the beiles shifted camp thirty li from the walls and sent one banner officer from each banner home ahead with five armored men per niru.

sentences.zh: 上遣濟爾哈朗代將，傳諭詰責，對曰：「臣以敵兵在錦州、松山、杏山三城，皆就他處牧馬。

translations.literal: The sovereign dispatched Jirhalang to replace him as commander and sent an edict of rebuke; [Dorgon] replied: "Your subject saw enemy troops at the three cities of Jinzhou, Songshan, and Xingshan, all grazing their horses elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: The khan sent Jirhalang to take command and rebuked him by edict. Dorgon answered: "The enemy holds Jinzhou, Songshan, and Xingshan, yet they pasture their horses far afield.

sentences.zh: 若來犯，可更番抵禦。

translations.literal: If they attack, we can rotate in defense.
translations.idiomatic: If they strike, we can relieve one another in turn.

sentences.zh: 是以遣人歸牧，治甲械。

translations.literal: Therefore I sent men back to pasture and to repair armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I sent men home to graze the herds and overhaul arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 舊駐地草盡，臣倡議移營就牧，罪實在臣。

translations.literal: The grass at our old encampment was exhausted; I proposed moving camp to better pasture—the fault is truly mine.
translations.idiomatic: Our old camp was grazed bare; I urged shifting to fresh pasture, and the blame is mine alone.

sentences.zh: 」上復使諭曰：「朕愛爾過於羣子弟，錫予獨厚。

translations.literal: " The sovereign again sent word: "I love you more than my other kinsmen and have rewarded you most generously.
translations.idiomatic: " The khan replied: "I favor you above my other nephews and have heaped gifts upon you.

sentences.zh: 今違命若此，其自議之。

translations.literal: Now that you have disobeyed orders in this way, consider the matter yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you have defied me thus—judge your own case.

sentences.zh: 」王自言罪當死，上命降郡王，罰銀萬，奪二牛錄。

translations.literal: " The Prince himself said the crime deserved death; the sovereign ordered his rank reduced to prince of a commandery, fined him ten thousand taels of silver, and confiscated two niru.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince pleaded that he deserved death. The khan demoted him to a commandery prince, fined him ten thousand taels, and stripped him of two niru.

sentences.zh: 六年，复圍錦州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, [he] again besieged Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he returned to the siege of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪承疇率十三萬人屯松山，王屢擊之，以敵馳六日，次戚家堡，將屯高橋。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou led one hundred thirty thousand men encamped at Songshan; the Prince repeatedly attacked him; after the enemy had marched six days they halted at Qijiapu and were about to encamp at Gaoqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou sat at Songshan with a hundred and thirty thousand men. The Prince harried him repeatedly; after six days on the march the Ming army paused at Qijiapu and prepared to camp at Gaoqiao.

sentences.zh: 王請上駐松山、杏山間，分兵屯烏欣河南山，亙海為營。

translations.literal: The Prince requested the sovereign to remain between Songshan and Xingshan, divide troops to encamp on the southern hills south of the Wuxin River, and establish camps stretching to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince urged the khan to hold the ground between Songshan and Xingshan, plant detachments on the hills south of the Wuxin River, and line the coast with camps.

sentences.zh: 明兵屢？

translations.literal: Ming forces repeatedly charged.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming lines charged again and again.

sentences.zh: 复前，上張黃葢指揮，明兵引退。

translations.literal: They charged once more; the sovereign raised the yellow canopy and directed [the battle], and the Ming forces withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When they surged forward again, the khan raised the yellow imperial canopy to direct the fight, and the Ming troops fell back.

sentences.zh: 王偕洛託等趨塔山道橫擊之，明兵多死者；

translations.literal: The Prince with Luotuo and others rushed along the Tashan road to strike them on the flank, and many Ming soldiers were killed;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince, Luotuo, and others swept along the Tashan road and caught the Ming column on the flank, leaving many dead;

sentences.zh: 遂發礮克塔山外四台，擒王希賢等。

translations.literal: they then opened fire with cannon, captured the four forts outside Tashan, and took Wang Xixian and others prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: then opened with cannon, took the four outworks beyond Tashan, and captured Wang Xixian and others.

sentences.zh: 尋以貝勒杜度等代將，王暫還，復出。

translations.literal: Soon Beile Dudu and others replaced him as commanders; the Prince temporarily returned, then went out again.
translations.idiomatic: Beile Dudu and others soon replaced him in command; the Prince withdrew briefly, then returned to the front.

sentences.zh: 七年，下松山，獲承疇，克錦州，大壽复降。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Songshan fell, Hong Chengchou was captured, Jinzhou was taken, and Zu Dashou surrendered again.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Songshan fell, Hong Chengchou was taken, Jinzhou capitulated, and Zu Dashou submitted once more.

sentences.zh: 進克塔山、杏山。

translations.literal: They then captured Tashan and Xingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Tashan and Xingshan followed.

sentences.zh: 乃墮三城，師還，敘功，復親王。

translations.literal: The three cities were then demolished; when the army returned, merits were reckoned and he was restored to imperial prince.
translations.idiomatic: The three fortresses were razed. After the campaign his honors were reviewed and his rank as an imperial prince was restored.

sentences.zh: 八年，太宗崩，王與諸王、貝勒、大臣奉世祖即位。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Taizong died; the Prince, together with princes, beiles, and ministers, installed Shizu on the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Hong Taiji died. The Prince, with the other princes, beiles, and ministers, enthroned Shizu.

sentences.zh: 諸王、貝勒、大臣議以鄭親王濟爾哈朗與王同輔政，誓曰：「有不秉公輔理、妄自尊大者，天地譴之！

translations.literal: The princes, beiles, and ministers resolved that Prince Zheng Jirhalang and the Prince should jointly assist in government, and swore: "Whoever does not assist justly in governing but arrogantly exalts himself—may Heaven condemn him!
translations.idiomatic: The princes, beiles, and ministers agreed that Prince Zheng Jirhalang and the Prince would share the regency, swearing: "Let Heaven punish any man who governs unjustly or sets himself above the rest!

sentences.zh: 」郡王阿達禮、貝子碩託勸王自立，王發其謀，誅阿達禮、碩託。

translations.literal: " Commandery Prince Adali and Beizi Situo urged the Prince to take the throne himself; the Prince exposed their plot and executed Adali and Situo.
translations.idiomatic: " Commandery Prince Adali and Beizi Situo then pressed him to seize the throne; he uncovered their conspiracy and put both men to death.

sentences.zh: 尋與濟爾哈朗議罷諸王貝勒管六部事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he and Jirhalang resolved to abolish the princes' and beiles' administration of the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: He and Jirhalang soon moved to end princely control of the Six Ministries.

sentences.zh: 順治元年正月，卻朝鮮餽遺，告濟爾哈朗及諸大臣曰：「朝鮮國王因予取江華，全其妻子，常以私餽遺。

translations.literal: In the first month of Shunzhi 1, he declined gifts from Korea and told Jirhalang and the ministers: "Because I took Ganghwa yet spared the king's wife and children, the Korean king has often sent me private gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Shunzhi 1 he refused Korean presents and told Jirhalang and the ministers: "When I seized Ganghwa I spared the king's family, and ever since the Korean king has tried to court me with private gifts.

sentences.zh: 先帝時必聞而受之，今輔政，誼無私交，不當受。

translations.literal: In the late emperor's time such things were heard of and accepted; now that I assist in government, there should be no private ties—I ought not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Under the late emperor such gifts were known and taken; as regent I may keep no private dealings, and I will not accept them.

sentences.zh: 」因並禁外國餽諸王貝勒者。

translations.literal: " He therefore also forbade foreign gifts to princes and beiles.
translations.idiomatic: " He likewise banned foreign tribute to any prince or beile.

sentences.zh: 濟爾哈朗諭諸大臣，凡事先白王，書名亦先之。

translations.literal: Jirhalang instructed the ministers that in all affairs they should first inform the Prince, and in signing documents his name should come first.
translations.idiomatic: Jirhalang ordered the ministers to clear every matter with the Prince first and to list his name ahead of all others on memorials.

sentences.zh: 王由是始專政。

translations.literal: From this the Prince began to monopolize government.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the Prince's personal rule began.

sentences.zh: 固山額真何洛會等訐肅親王豪格怨望，集議，削爵，大臣揚善等以諂附，坐死。

translations.literal: Gushan ejen He Lohui and others denounced Prince Su Hooge for resentment; at a council his title was stripped, and ministers Yang Shan and others, for fawning complicity, were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Gushan ejen He Lohui and others accused Prince Su Hooge of disloyal muttering; the council stripped his rank, and ministers such as Yang Shan were executed for currying favor with him.

sentences.zh: 四月乙丑，上御篤恭殿，授王奉命大將軍印，並御用纛蓋，敕便宜行事，率武英郡王阿濟格、豫郡王多鐸及孔有德等伐明。

translations.literal: On yichou, the fourth month, the sovereign attended at the Dugong Hall, conferred on the Prince the seal of Grand General by Imperial Command together with the imperial banner and canopy, authorized him to act at discretion, and ordered him to lead Prince Wuying Ajige, Prince Yu Dodo, and Kong Youde and others against Ming.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou in the fourth month the young emperor appeared at the Dugong Hall, invested the Prince with the seal of Grand General by Imperial Command and the imperial banner and canopy, empowered him to act on his own authority, and dispatched him with Prince Wuying Ajige, Prince Yu Dodo, Kong Youde, and others to march against Ming.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，發盛京。

translations.literal: On bingyin, [the army] departed Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the army left Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 壬申，次翁後。

translations.literal: On renshen, [they] halted at Weng'hou.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen they encamped at Weng'hou.

sentences.zh: 明平西伯吳三桂自山海關來書乞師，王得書，移師向之。

translations.literal: Ming Prince of the West Wu Sangui wrote from Shanhaiguan begging for troops; the Prince received the letter and shifted the army toward him.
translations.idiomatic: From Shanhaiguan the Ming Prince of the West, Wu Sangui, sent a letter pleading for relief; the Prince read it and turned his march toward the pass.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，次西拉塔拉。

translations.literal: On guiyou, [they] halted at Xilatala.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou they halted at Xilatala.

sentences.zh: 答三桂書曰：「我國欲與明修好，屢致書不一答。

translations.literal: In reply to Sangui's letter he wrote: "Our state wished to make peace with Ming and repeatedly sent letters, yet received no answer.
translations.idiomatic: He answered Sangui: "We sought friendship with Ming and wrote again and again, but no reply ever came.

sentences.zh: 是以整師三入，蓋示意於明，欲其熟籌通好。

translations.literal: Therefore we marshaled our armies and entered three times, intending to show Ming our meaning and move them to consider friendly relations carefully.
translations.idiomatic: That is why we marched in three great invasions—to make our intentions plain and press Ming to weigh an alliance.

sentences.zh: 今則不復出此，惟底定中原，與民休息而已。

translations.literal: Now we no longer speak of that; we seek only to settle the Central Plains and let the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: That talk is behind us now; our aim is to pacify the Central Plains and give the people peace.

sentences.zh: 聞流賊陷京都，崇禎帝慘亡，不勝髮指，用率仁義之師，沈舟破釜，誓必滅賊，出民水火！

translations.literal: Hearing that the bandit army has taken the capital and that Emperor Chongzhen has died a tragic death, I cannot contain my rage; therefore I lead an army of benevolence and righteousness, having burned our boats and smashed our cooking pots, swearing that we must exterminate the bandits and deliver the people from flood and fire!
translations.idiomatic: When I learned that the rebel host had seized the capital and that Emperor Chongzhen had met a cruel end, my hair stood on end with fury. I now lead an army of righteousness with boats burned and kettles shattered, vowing to destroy the rebels and pull the people out of fire and water!

sentences.zh: 伯思報主恩，與流賊不共戴天，誠忠臣之義，勿因向守遼東與我為敵，尚復來歸，必封以故土，晉為籓？

translations.literal: You, my lord, think to repay your sovereign's grace; you share with the bandits a hatred that brooks no coexistence—this is truly the duty of a loyal minister. Do not let the fact that you once held Liaodong against us keep you from returning; if you come back, you will surely be enfeoffed with your former lands and advanced to princely rank as a vassal—
translations.idiomatic: You seek to repay your lord's kindness and cannot live under the same sky as the rebels—that is the mark of a true loyalist. Do not let your old defense of Liaodong against us keep you away; if you return, your former domain will be restored and you will be raised to princely rank as a feudatory—

sentences.zh: 懷疑。

translations.literal: do not doubt it.
translations.idiomatic: have no doubt of it.

sentences.zh: 昔管仲射桓公中鉤，桓公用為仲父，以成霸業。

translations.literal: In former times Guan Zhong's arrow struck Duke Huan and pierced his belt hook, yet Duke Huan made him his zhongfu and thereby achieved hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Guan Zhong's arrow struck Duke Huan's belt hook, yet the duke made him his chief minister and so built a hegemony.

sentences.zh: 伯若率王。

translations.literal: If you, my lord, lead princes, nobles, officers, and soldiers to come over,
translations.idiomatic: If you, my lord, bring princes, nobles, officers, and soldiers to our side,

sentences.zh: 國讎可報，身家可保，世世子孫，長享富貴。

translations.literal: national vengeance can be avenged, your person and household can be preserved, and your descendants for generations will long enjoy wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: the nation's wrong can be avenged, your house can be saved, and your children and grandchildren will enjoy wealth and honor for generations.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，次連山。

translations.literal: On dingchou, [they] halted at Lianshan.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou they camped at Lianshan.

sentences.zh: 三桂復遣使請速進，夜逾寧遠抵沙河。

translations.literal: Sangui again sent envoys asking for a rapid advance; [they] traveled by night past Ningyuan and reached Shahe.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui sent again, begging haste; the envoys rode through the night past Ningyuan to Shahe.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，距關十里，三桂報自成兵已出邊。

translations.literal: On wuyin, ten li from the pass, Sangui reported that Li Zicheng's army had already left the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, ten li from the pass, Sangui reported that Li Zicheng's force had already marched out.

sentences.zh: 王令諸王逆擊，敗李自成將唐通於一片石。

translations.literal: The Prince ordered the princes to intercept and attack, and Li Zicheng's general Tang Tong was defeated at Yipianshi.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince ordered the princes forward to intercept; at Yipianshi they routed Li Zicheng's general Tang Tong.

sentences.zh: 己卯，至山海關，三桂出迎，王慰勞之。

translations.literal: On jimao, [they] reached Shanhaiguan; Sangui came out to welcome them, and the Prince comforted and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao they reached Shanhaiguan. Sangui came out to meet them, and the Prince praised and reassured him.

sentences.zh: 令所部以白布系肩為識，先驅入關。

translations.literal: He ordered his troops to tie white cloth on their shoulders as a mark and advance into the pass first.
translations.idiomatic: He told his men to bind white cloth on their shoulders for recognition and sent them through the pass ahead of the main body.

sentences.zh: 時自成將二十餘萬人，自北山列陣，橫亙至海。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zicheng had more than two hundred thousand men, drawn up in battle array from the northern hills in a line stretching to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng then had more than two hundred thousand men, deployed from the northern hills in a battle line that ran all the way to the shore.

sentences.zh: 我兵陳不及海岸，王令曰：「流賊橫行久，獷而。

translations.literal: Our battle line did not reach the coast; the Prince ordered: "The bandits have run rampant for long and are fierce and prone to underestimate the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Our line fell short of the coast. The Prince said: "These rebels have swaggered for years—they are fierce and careless of their foe.

sentences.zh: 可集我軍鱗比，伺敵陣尾，待其衰擊之，必勝。

translations.literal: Gather our troops in close formation, watch the enemy's rear, and strike when they flag—we are sure to win.
translations.idiomatic: Mass our men shoulder to shoulder, watch the enemy's flank and rear, and hit them when their strength fades—we will win.

sentences.zh: 努力破此，大業成矣。

translations.literal: Break them with all your might and the great enterprise is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Break them here with all your strength, and the great work is done.

sentences.zh: 勿違節制！

translations.literal: Do not disobey command!
translations.idiomatic: Do not break ranks!

sentences.zh: 」既成列，令三桂居右翼後。

translations.literal: " Once the lines were formed, he ordered Sangui to take position behind the right wing.
translations.idiomatic: " When the armies were drawn up, he placed Sangui behind the right wing.

sentences.zh: 搏戰，大風揚沙，咫尺不能辨。

translations.literal: In the fighting a great wind raised sand, and at arm's length one could not tell friend from foe.
translations.idiomatic: As the battle joined, a gale whipped up sand until men a spear-length apart could barely see one another.

sentences.zh: 力突出，搗其中堅，馬迅矢激。

translations.literal: They charged out with full force and struck the enemy center; horses were swift and arrows flew fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: They drove forward with all their strength, punching into the enemy center; horses flew and arrows darkened the air.

sentences.zh: 自成登高望見，奪氣，策馬走。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng watched from high ground, lost heart, whipped his horse, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng looked down from a height, lost his nerve, and bolted on horseback.

sentences.zh: 師無不一當百，追奔四十里，自成潰遁。

translations.literal: Every man in the army fought as one against a hundred; they pursued the rout for forty li, and Li Zicheng fled in collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Every soldier fought as if he were worth a hundred men; they chased the broken army forty li, and Li Zicheng fled in utter rout.

sentences.zh: 王即軍前承製進三桂爵平西王。

translations.literal: The Prince immediately before the army received the imperial decree and advanced Sangui to Prince of the West.
translations.idiomatic: There on the field the Prince received the imperial patent and created Sangui Prince of the West.

sentences.zh: 下令關內軍民皆薙髪。

translations.literal: He ordered that all soldiers and civilians within the pass shave their heads.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded every soldier and civilian inside the pass to shave the head in the queue.

sentences.zh: 以馬步兵各萬人屬三桂，追擊自成。

translations.literal: He assigned ten thousand cavalry and infantry to Sangui to pursue Li Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Sangui ten thousand horse and foot to hunt Li Zicheng down.

sentences.zh: 乃誓諸將曰：「此行除暴救民，滅賊以安天下。

translations.literal: He then swore to the generals: "On this expedition we suppress violence and save the people, destroying the bandits to settle the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He then took an oath with his commanders: "This march is to crush tyranny and rescue the people—to destroy the rebels and bring peace to the realm.

sentences.zh: 勿殺無辜、掠財物、焚廬舍。

translations.literal: Do not kill the innocent, plunder goods, or burn dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Spare the innocent. Take no plunder. Burn no homes.

sentences.zh: 不如約者，罪之。

translations.literal: Whoever does not keep to this agreement will be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever breaks this pledge will answer for it.

sentences.zh: 」自關以西，百姓有逃竄山谷者，皆還鄉里，薙髪迎降。

translations.literal: " West of the pass, common people who had fled into the mountains all returned to their villages, shaved their heads, and welcomed surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " Beyond the pass, villagers who had hidden in the hills came home, shaved their heads, and submitted.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，次新河驛，使奏捷，師遂進。

translations.literal: On xinsi, [they] newly arrived at Xinhe Post, sent in a victory report, and the army then advanced.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi they reached Xinhe Post, dispatched word of victory, and pressed on.

sentences.zh: 途中明將吏出降，命供職如故。

translations.literal: Along the way Ming generals and officials came out to surrender; [he] ordered them to retain their posts as before.
translations.idiomatic: As they marched, Ming commanders and officials surrendered in droves; the Prince ordered them to keep their offices unchanged.

sentences.zh: 五月戊子朔，師次通州。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, wuzi, the army halted at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month (wuzi), the army encamped at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 自成先一日焚宮闕，載輜重而西。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng one day earlier had burned the palace halls, loaded the baggage train, and [went] west.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng had burned the palace the day before and was already heading west with his supply train.

sentences.zh: 王令諸王偕三桂各率所部追之。

translations.literal: The Prince ordered the various princes together with Sangui each to lead their respective divisions in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince ordered the princes, together with Sangui, each to lead his command in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 己丑，王整軍入京師，明將吏軍民迎朝陽門外，設鹵簿，請乘輦，王曰：「予法周公輔沖王，不當乘。

translations.literal: On jichou, the Prince regrouped the army and entered the capital. Ming generals, officials, soldiers, and civilians received [him] outside Chaoyang Gate, set up the imperial insignia, and requested that he take the palanquin. The Prince said: "I take the Duke of Zhou as my model in assisting the young sovereign; I ought not to ride.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the Prince brought his army in order and entered the capital. Ming officers, troops, and townspeople received him outside Chaoyang Gate with full imperial regalia and asked him to take the imperial palanquin. The Prince said, "I mean to assist the young emperor as the Duke of Zhou did; I am not entitled to ride.

sentences.zh: 」以周公嘗負扆，固請，乃命以鹵簿列王儀仗前，奏樂，拜天，復拜闕，乘輦，升武英殿。

translations.literal: " Because the Duke of Zhou once had borne the imperial screen, [they] pressed insistently; thereupon he ordered the imperial insignia to be arrayed before the Prince's guard of honor, music was played, he bowed to Heaven, bowed again toward the palace, took the palanquin, and ascended the Hall of Martial Glory.
translations.idiomatic: " They urged that the Duke of Zhou had once stood at the screen behind the throne, and would not desist; at last he had the imperial regalia placed ahead of his own escort, music sounded, and he bowed to Heaven and then to the palace before mounting the palanquin and entering the Hall of Martial Glory.

sentences.zh: 」明將吏入謁，呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Ming generals and officials entered to pay homage and shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: Ming officers came to audience and shouted "Long live!"

sentences.zh: 下令將士皆乘城，毋入民舍，民安堵如故。

translations.literal: He ordered the soldiers all to man the walls and not enter private dwellings; the people lived undisturbed as before.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the troops to hold the walls and stay out of private homes, and the people went about their lives as before.

sentences.zh: 為崇禎帝發喪三日，具帝禮葬之。

translations.literal: For Emperor Chongzhen he proclaimed mourning for three days and buried him with full imperial rites.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered three days of mourning for Emperor Chongzhen and laid him to rest with full imperial ceremony.

sentences.zh: 諸臣降者，仍以明官治事。

translations.literal: Those among the officials who had surrendered continued to carry out affairs in their former Ming posts.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered officials were kept at their Ming posts to govern as before.

sentences.zh: 武英郡王阿濟格逐自成至慶都，大破之，獲其輜重。

translations.literal: Prince Wuying Ajige pursued Li Zicheng to Qingdu, routed him utterly, and captured his baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wuying Ajige chased Li Zicheng to Qingdu, crushed his army, and seized his supply train.

sentences.zh: 自成西奔，又令固山額真譚泰、準塔等率巴牙喇兵追至真定，自成敗走。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng fled west; [the Prince] again ordered the banners ejen Tan Tai, Zhunta, and others to lead the Baturu troops in pursuit to Zhending, where Li Zicheng was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng bolted westward; the Prince sent the banners ejen Tan Tai, Zhunta, and others with the Baturu guard in pursuit to Zhending, where Li Zicheng was beaten and driven off again.

sentences.zh: 巴泰齎敕慰勞。

translations.literal: Batai carried an edict of consolation and commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Batai was sent with an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 畿輔諸府縣先後請降，分遣固山額真巴哈納、石廷柱略山東，葉臣定山西諸省，金礪等安撫天津。

translations.literal: The prefectures and districts of the capital region successively offered surrender; he dispatched separately the banners ejen Bahana and Shi Tingzhu to pacify Shandong, Ye Chen to settle the provinces of Shanxi, and Jin Li and others to reassure Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: The capital districts surrendered one after another. He sent Bahana and Shi Tingzhu into Shandong, Ye Chen to secure Shanxi, and Jin Li and others to pacify Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 王初令官民皆薙髪，繼聞拂民願，諭緩之。

translations.literal: The Prince at first ordered officials and commoners all to shave their heads; on later hearing that this ran against the people's wishes, he proclaimed that it would be deferred.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince first commanded every official and subject to shave the head; when he learned it offended popular sentiment, he announced a postponement.

sentences.zh: 令戒飭官吏，網羅賢才，收卹都市貧民。

translations.literal: He ordered that officials be warned and disciplined, talented men be gathered, and poor people in the cities be relieved and cared for.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed officials to behave with restraint, recruit able men, and provide relief for the urban poor.

sentences.zh: 用湯若望議，釐正曆法，定名曰時憲歷。

translations.literal: Following Adam Schall's proposal, he revised and rectified the calendar system, fixing its name as the Shixian Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: On Adam Schall's recommendation he reformed the calendar and named it the Shixian Calendar.

sentences.zh: 復令曰：「養民之道，莫大於省刑罰，薄稅斂。

translations.literal: He again issued an edict: "In nurturing the people, nothing is greater than reducing punishments and lightening taxes and levies.
translations.idiomatic: He issued another decree: "To nurture the people, nothing matters more than easing punishments and lightening taxes.

sentences.zh: 自明季禍亂，刁風日競，設機構訟，敗俗傷財，心竊痛之！

translations.literal: Since the catastrophes and chaos of the late Ming, devious practices grew more fierce by the day; fabricating schemes and stirring litigation ruined customs and wasted wealth—I have privately been pained at heart!
translations.idiomatic: Since the late Ming collapse, sharp practices and vexatious lawsuits have only grown worse, ruining public morals and draining the people's wealth. This pains me deeply.

sentences.zh: 自今咸與維新，凡五月初二日昧爽，以前罪無大小，悉行宥免。

translations.literal: From now let all be renewed together: as of dawn on the second day of the fifth month, all crimes great and small committed before that hour are wholly pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all shall begin anew: every offense committed before dawn on the second day of the fifth month, whatever its gravity, is hereby forgiven.

sentences.zh: 違諭訐訟，以所告罪罪之。

translations.literal: Whoever disobeys this edict and brings malicious suits shall be punished with the offense of which he accuses [others].
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who defies this order and brings malicious litigation shall be punished for the very crime he alleges.

sentences.zh: 重大者經撫按結案，非機密要情，毋許入京越訴。

translations.literal: Major cases must be concluded through the provincial and surveillance commissioners; unless they involve confidential matters of high importance, appeals to the capital are not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Important cases must be settled by the provincial authorities; appeals to Beijing are forbidden except for urgent matters of state secrecy.

sentences.zh: 訟師誣陷良民，加等反坐。

translations.literal: Pettifoggers who falsely entrap upright commoners shall suffer enhanced penalties in counter-charge.
translations.idiomatic: Legal schemers who frame honest citizens shall face aggravated punishment under the law of counter-charge.

sentences.zh: 前朝弊政，莫如加派，遼餉之外，復有剿餉、練餉，數倍正供，遠者二十年，近者十餘年，天下嗷嗷，朝不及夕。

translations.literal: Among the corrupt policies of the former dynasty, none was worse than surcharged levies: beyond the Liaodong ration there were again suppression and training rations, several times the regular quota; for as much as twenty years in some places and more than ten in others—the realm groaned in distress, with each morning not knowing whether there would be an evening.
translations.idiomatic: No Ming abuse was worse than the supplemental levies—on top of the Liaodong surcharge came the suppression and training surcharges, multiplying the normal tax. Some regions endured this for twenty years, others for more than ten, until the land cried out in misery and families could not be sure of living from one morning to the next.

sentences.zh: 更有召買、糧料諸名目，巧取殃民。

translations.literal: There were moreover such designations as compulsory purchase and grain fees, cunningly extracted to bring calamity upon the people.
translations.idiomatic: Under names like compulsory purchase and grain surcharges, officials invented still more devices to wring the people dry.

sentences.zh: 今與民約，額賦外，一切加派，盡予刪除。

translations.literal: Now I make this pact with the people: beyond the fixed land tax, all surcharged levies shall be wholly abolished.
translations.idiomatic: From this day I pledge to the people: every surcharge beyond the fixed land tax is abolished.

sentences.zh: 官吏不從，察實治罪。

translations.literal: If officials do not comply, upon verified investigation they will be punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who defy this order will be investigated and punished.

sentences.zh: 」六月，遣輔國公屯齊喀、和託，固山額真何洛會等迎上，定都燕京。

translations.literal: " In the sixth month he dispatched the Assistant Prince Tunqiqi and Hoton, the banners ejen Hošoi, and others to welcome the sovereign, and fixed the capital at Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: " In the sixth month he sent Tunqiqi, Hoton, Hošoi, and others to escort the young emperor south and made Yanjing the capital.

sentences.zh: 明福王由崧稱帝江寧，遣其大學士史可法督師揚州，設江北四鎮，沿淮、徐置戍。

translations.literal: Ming's Prince of Fu, Zhu Yousong, proclaimed himself emperor at Jiangning; he dispatched his grand secretary Shi Kefa to command forces at Yangzhou, established the four garrisons of Jiangbei, and posted guards along the Huai and Xu [regions].
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yousong, the Ming Prince of Fu, declared himself emperor at Jiangning. He sent Grand Secretary Shi Kefa to take command at Yangzhou, organized the four Jiangbei garrisons, and posted defenses along the Huai and Xu line.

sentences.zh: 王致書可法曰：「予向在瀋陽，即知燕京物望，咸推司馬。

translations.literal: The Prince wrote to Kefa: "When I was still at Shenyang, I already knew that in Yanjing men's esteem was united in commending the Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince wrote to Shi Kefa: "Even when I was in Shenyang, I knew how highly men in Yanjing thought of you—they all spoke of you as the Marshal.

sentences.zh: 後入關破賊，得與都人士相接，識介弟於清班，曾託其手勒平安，拳致衷緒，未審以何時得達。

translations.literal: Later, entering the pass and defeating the bandits, I was able to meet with gentlemen of the capital and came to know your younger brother among the Qing ranks; I once entrusted him with a hand-written note wishing peace, earnestly conveying my heartfelt feelings—I do not know at what time it reached you.
translations.idiomatic: After I entered the pass and defeated the rebels, I met many men of the capital and came to know your younger brother in our ranks. I asked him to carry a letter wishing you well, with all sincerity—but I do not know when, or whether, it ever reached you.

sentences.zh: 比聞道路紛紛，多謂金陵有自立者。

translations.literal: Recently I have heard much rumor on the roads, with many saying that at Jinling someone has set himself up [as ruler].
translations.idiomatic: Lately the roads have buzzed with rumor that Jinling has raised a rival sovereign.

sentences.zh: 夫君父之仇，不共戴天。

translations.literal: Alas—the debt owed to one's sovereign and father is one that cannot be borne under the same sky.
translations.idiomatic: The murder of one's sovereign and father is a hatred that cannot be shared under heaven.

sentences.zh: 春秋之義，有賊不討，則故君不得書葬，新君不得書即位，所以防亂臣賊子，法至嚴也。

translations.literal: The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals is this: if rebels are not punished, the former ruler may not be recorded as buried and the new ruler may not be recorded as ascending the throne—this is how treacherous ministers and rebellious sons are guarded against; the law is exceedingly strict.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn tradition is clear: until rebels are punished, the old ruler cannot be duly buried in the record nor the new ruler properly enthroned. That is how the canon restrains traitors—the standard could not be sterner.

sentences.zh: 闖賊李自成，稱兵犯闕，手毒君親，中國臣民，不聞加遺一矢。

translations.literal: The rebel bandit Li Zicheng raised arms, violated the palace, and with his own hand did violence to the sovereign and the royal parents; yet among the subjects of China none is heard to have sent forth so much as a single arrow [against him].
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng the rebel raised rebellion, stormed the palace, and with his own hand killed the emperor and empress—yet not one subject of China is said to have loosed a single arrow against him.

sentences.zh: 平西王吳三桂，介在東陲，獨效包胥之哭，朝廷感其忠義，念累世之宿好，棄近日之小嫌，爰整貔貅，驅除狗鼠。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui, Prince of the West, stationed on the eastern frontier alone imitated Bao Xu's weeping lament; the court was moved by his loyalty and righteousness, recalled the friendship of generations, set aside recent petty grievances, and therefore marshaled its armies and drove off dogs and rats.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui, Prince of the West, alone on the far northeast played the part of Shen Baoxu in desperate appeal. Our court honored his loyalty, remembered the friendship of generations, and put recent quarrels aside—then we marched in force and swept the vermin away.

sentences.zh: 入京之日，首崇帝后諡號，卜葬山陵，悉如典禮。

translations.literal: On the day of entering the capital, we first honored the posthumous titles of the emperor and empress, selected burial mounds and interred them, all according to canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The day we entered the capital we first restored the posthumous honors of the late emperor and empress and laid them to rest in imperial tombs by full rite.

sentences.zh: 親郡王、將軍以下，一仍故封，不加改削。

translations.literal: Imperial princes, commandery princes, generals, and ranks below—all retained their former enfeoffments without alteration or reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and generals of every rank kept their former titles without diminution.

sentences.zh: 勳戚文武諸臣，咸在朝列，恩禮有加。

translations.literal: Meritorious kinsmen and civil and military officials all stood in the court ranks, receiving added grace and courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Nobles and civil and military officers alike remain at court, treated with added honor.

sentences.zh: 耕市不驚，秋毫無擾。

translations.literal: Ploughing and markets were undisturbed; not a hair's breadth was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Fields were tilled and markets stayed open—not a blade of grass was touched.

sentences.zh: 方擬秋高氣爽，遣將西征；

translations.literal: We were just planning, when the autumn air is high and clear, to dispatch generals on a western expedition;
translations.idiomatic: We were preparing, once the autumn air turned clear and crisp, to send generals westward;

sentences.zh: 傳檄江南，聯兵河朔，陳師鞠旅，戮力同心，報乃君國之仇，彰我朝廷之德。

translations.literal: to issue a proclamation to Jiangnan, join forces with Hebei and Shandong, array the army and drill the troops, unite strength with one heart, avenge the debt owed to your sovereign and state, and display the virtue of our court.
translations.idiomatic: to proclaim our cause in the south, join arms with the north, marshal our forces, and with one heart avenge your lord's death and display our court's virtue.

sentences.zh: 豈意南州諸君子，苟安旦夕，弗審事機，聊慕虛名，頓忘實害，予甚惑之！

translations.literal: Who could have expected that the gentlemen of the southern provinces would seek comfort day to day, fail to discern the moment's opportunity, briefly chase empty reputation, and suddenly forget real harm—I am greatly perplexed!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the gentlemen of the south seem content with each passing day, blind to the tides of events, chasing hollow fame while forgetting real peril. I am deeply puzzled!

sentences.zh: 國家撫定燕都，得之於闖賊，非取之於明朝也。

translations.literal: Our state pacified and settled Yanjing; we obtained it from the rebel bandit, not by taking it from the Ming dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Our state has pacified Yanjing—we took it from the rebels, not from the Ming.

sentences.zh: 賊毀明朝之廟主，辱及先人，我國家不憚徵繕之勞，悉索敝賦，代為雪恥，孝子仁人，當如何感恩圖報。

translations.literal: The bandits destroyed the Ming ancestral tablets and shamed our forebears; our state did not shrink from the toil of raising armies, exhausted its depleted resources, and avenged the shame on your behalf—filial sons and humane men, how ought they to feel gratitude and seek repayment?
translations.idiomatic: The rebels desecrated the Ming ancestral shrines and humiliated your dead. Our state spared neither expense nor effort to avenge that shame on your behalf. What filial son or humane gentleman would not feel bound to repay such a debt?

sentences.zh: 茲乃乘逆寇稽誅，王師暫息，遂欲雄據江南，坐享漁人之利。

translations.literal: Yet now, taking advantage of the rebel chieftain's delay in execution and the temporary pause of the royal army, you wish to hold Jiangnan in overbearing dominance and sit enjoying the fisherman's profit.
translations.idiomatic: And now, while rebels still evade final punishment and our armies pause to regroup, you would seize Jiangnan for yourselves and play the fisherman watching others fight.

sentences.zh: 揆諸情理，豈可謂平？

translations.literal: Weighing this against reason and feeling, can it be called fair?
translations.idiomatic: By any measure of reason, can this be called just?

sentences.zh: 將以為天塹不能飛渡，投鞭不能斷流耶？

translations.literal: Do you suppose the heaven-sent moat cannot be flown across, or that a whip cast into the river cannot break its flow?
translations.idiomatic: Do you imagine the Yangtze cannot be crossed, that a thrown whip can break its current?

sentences.zh: 夫闖賊但為明朝祟耳，未嘗得罪於我國家也，徒以薄海同仇，特伸大義。

translations.literal: Now the rebel bandit was merely a bane to the Ming; he never offended our state. Only because all within the seas shared the same enemy did we specially extend great righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel troubled the Ming alone; he had done our state no wrong. We acted only because all under heaven shared the enmity, extending justice on principle.

sentences.zh: 今若擁號稱尊，便是天有二日，儼為勍敵。

translations.literal: If now you hold up a title and proclaim yourselves sovereign, it will be as though heaven had two suns—you will plainly be fierce enemies.
translations.idiomatic: If you now proclaim an emperor of your own, there will be two suns in the sky—and you will be our declared enemies.

sentences.zh: 予將簡西行之銳，轉旝東征，且擬釋彼重誅，命為前導。

translations.literal: I shall select the keen troops bound for the west, turn the standard east to campaign, and moreover intend to remit their heavy punishment and appoint them as advance guides.
translations.idiomatic: I shall withdraw the elite forces I had meant for the west and turn them eastward, and I even propose to lift the heavy sentences on them and appoint them as our vanguard.

sentences.zh: 夫以中華全力，受制潢池，而欲以江左一隅，兼支大國，勝負之數，無待蓍龜矣。

translations.literal: Now that the full strength of China has been held captive by the rebellious pool, yet one wishes to support a great state with only a corner of the lands east of the Yangtze—the issue of victory and defeat needs no divination with milfoil and tortoise shell.
translations.idiomatic: When all China's strength has been pinned down by rebellion, can a single stretch east of the Yangtze bear the weight of a great empire? The outcome scarcely needs an oracle to tell.

sentences.zh: 予聞君子之愛人也以德，細人則以姑息。

translations.literal: I have heard that the gentleman loves others through virtue, while the petty man does so through indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the gentleman cares for others through virtue, while the petty man does so through indulgence.

sentences.zh: 諸君子果識時知命，篤念故主，厚愛賢王，宜勸令削號歸籓，永綏福祿。

translations.literal: If you gentlemen truly know the times and accept fate, are deeply mindful of the former sovereign, and hold deep affection for the worthy prince, you ought to urge him to renounce his title and return to vassalage, securing lasting rank and blessings forever.
translations.idiomatic: If you gentlemen truly read the times and accept heaven's decree, hold fast to loyalty toward your former sovereign, and care deeply for that worthy prince, you ought to urge him to renounce his imperial title and return to vassalage, securing lasting rank and blessings.

sentences.zh: 朝廷當待以虞賓，統承禮物，帶礪山河，位在諸王侯上，庶不負朝廷伸義討賊、興滅繼絕之初心。

translations.literal: The court would receive him as Yu's guest, continue the customary gifts, grant him mountains and rivers bound by iron girdle and whetstone, and rank him above all princes and marquises—thus not failing the court's original purpose of upholding justice, punishing the rebel, and restoring what was lost.
translations.idiomatic: The court would receive him as an honored guest in the manner of Yu, continue the customary gifts, grant him an eternal fief with mountains and rivers as his bounds, and rank him above all other princes and marquises—thus fulfilling the court's original purpose of upholding justice, punishing the rebel, and restoring what was lost.

sentences.zh: 至南州羣彥，翩然來儀，則爾公爾侯，列爵分土，有平西之典例在。

translations.literal: As for the worthies of the southern provinces, should they come gracefully to join us, then duke for you and marquis for you—enfeoffment and lands apportioned—there is the precedent of the Pacifier of the West to follow.
translations.idiomatic: As for the worthies of the southern provinces, should you come gracefully to join us, offices of duke and marquis, enfeoffment and lands—there is the precedent of the Prince of the West to follow.

sentences.zh: 惟執事實圖利之！

translations.literal: I trust Your Excellency will truly weigh this to advantage!
translations.idiomatic: I trust Your Excellency will weigh this to real advantage!

sentences.zh: 輓近士大夫好高樹名義，而不顧國家之急，每有大事，輒同築舍。

translations.literal: Lately scholars have been fond of standing on high moral ground without regard for the state's urgent need; whenever a great matter arises, they argue endlessly like men building a house together.
translations.idiomatic: Lately scholars have been keen to stand on high moral ground without heed to the empire's urgent need; whenever a great matter arises, they argue endlessly like men building a house together.

sentences.zh: 昔宋人議論未定，兵已渡河，可為殷鑑。

translations.literal: Formerly the Song debated without reaching a decision while the enemy's army had already crossed the river—this may serve as a warning from the past.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Song debated until their armies were already across the river—a warning that should not be forgotten.

sentences.zh: 先生領袖名流，主持至計，必能深惟終始，寧忍隨俗浮沉？

translations.literal: You, sir, lead the eminent of the age and hold the decisive counsel; you must surely ponder matters through from first to last—how could you bear to drift with the tide?
translations.idiomatic: You, sir, lead the best minds of the age and hold the decisive counsel in your hands—you must surely ponder matters through from first to last; how could you bear to drift with the tide?

sentences.zh: 取捨從違，應早審定。

translations.literal: Whether to follow or resist should be decided early.
translations.idiomatic: Whether to follow or resist—this should be settled early.

sentences.zh: 兵行在即，可西可東。

translations.literal: The army will move shortly; it may go west or east.
translations.idiomatic: The army will move shortly; it may march west or east.

sentences.zh: 南國安危，在此一舉。

translations.literal: The safety of the southern state hangs on this single move.
translations.idiomatic: The survival of the southern realm hangs on this single decision.

sentences.zh: 原諸君子同以討賊為心，毋貪一身瞬息之榮，而重故國無窮之禍，為亂臣賊子所竊笑，予實有厚望焉！

translations.literal: I beg you gentlemen to join in heart in punishing the rebel, not grasp at a moment's personal glory and thereby heap endless disaster upon your former state, becoming the secret laughingstock of traitors—I truly place great hope in this!
translations.idiomatic: I beg you gentlemen to join in heart in punishing the rebel, not grasp at a moment's personal glory and thereby heap endless disaster upon your former state, becoming the secret laughingstock of traitors—this is my earnest hope!

sentences.zh: 記有之，惟善人能受盡言。

translations.literal: The records say that only the good man can receive words spoken to the full.
translations.idiomatic: The records say that only the good man can receive words spoken to the full.

sentences.zh: 敬布腹心，佇聞明教。

translations.literal: Respectfully I lay bare my inmost thoughts and await your enlightened instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully I lay bare my inmost thoughts and await your enlightened reply.

sentences.zh: 江天在望，延跂為勞，書不宣意。

translations.literal: The river and sky lie before me; straining to look upon them fills me with longing, and this letter cannot convey all I mean.
translations.idiomatic: The river and sky lie before me; straining to look upon them fills me with longing, and this letter cannot convey all I mean.

sentences.zh: 」可法旋遣人報書，語多不屈。

translations.literal: " Shi Kefa soon sent someone with a reply; his words were largely defiant.
translations.idiomatic: " Kefa soon sent a reply; his language was largely defiant.

sentences.zh: 京師民訛言秋​​七、八月將東遷，王宣諭當建都燕京，戒民毋信流言搖​​惑。

translations.literal: In the capital the people spread a false rumor that in the seventh or eighth month of autumn [the court] would move east again; the Prince issued a proclamation that the capital would be established at Yanjing and warned the people not to believe rumors meant to unsettle them.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital rumor spread that in the seventh or eighth month of autumn the court would move east again. The Prince issued a proclamation that the capital was to be established at Yanjing and warned the people not to believe rumors meant to unsettle them.

sentences.zh: 又訛言八月屠民；

translations.literal: There was also a false rumor that in the eighth month the populace would be massacred;
translations.idiomatic: There was also a rumor that in the eighth month the populace would be massacred;

sentences.zh: 未幾，又訛言上至京師，將縱東兵肆掠，盡殺老壯，止存孩赤。

translations.literal: Before long there was again a false rumor that when the Emperor reached the capital he would let eastern troops plunder at will, slaughtering every adult and leaving only children.
translations.idiomatic: Before long another rumor claimed that when the Emperor reached the capital he would let eastern troops plunder at will, slaughtering every adult and leaving only children.

sentences.zh: 王復宣諭曰：「民乃國之本，爾曹既誠心歸服，復以何罪而戮之？

translations.literal: The Prince issued another proclamation, saying: "The people are the foundation of the state. Since you have submitted in good faith, on what charge would we slaughter you?
translations.idiomatic: The Prince issued another proclamation: "The people are the foundation of the state. Since you have submitted in good faith, on what charge would we slaughter you?

sentences.zh: 爾曹試思，今上攜將士家屬不下億萬，與之俱來者何故？

translations.literal: Consider: the present Emperor has brought with him the households of soldiers and officers—no fewer than a hundred million people—why have they all come?
translations.idiomatic: Consider: the present Emperor has brought with him the households of soldiers and officers—no fewer than a hundred million people—why have they all come?

sentences.zh: 為安燕京軍民也。

translations.literal: To settle Yanjing and secure the army and people.
translations.idiomatic: To settle Yanjing and secure the army and people.

sentences.zh: 昨將東來各官內，命十餘員為督、撫、司、道等官者何故？

translations.literal: Yesterday, among the officials sent from the east, why were more than ten appointed governors, provincial commissioners, and circuit intendants?
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, among the officials sent from the east, why were more than ten appointed governors, provincial commissioners, and the like?

sentences.zh: 為統一天下也。

translations.literal: To unify the empire under one rule.
translations.idiomatic: To unify the empire under one rule.

sentences.zh: 已將盛京帑銀取至百餘萬，後又轉運不絕者何故？

translations.literal: Why has more than a million taels of treasury silver been brought from Mukden, with shipments continuing without cease?
translations.idiomatic: Why has more than a million taels of treasury silver been brought from Mukden, with shipments continuing without cease?

sentences.zh: 為供爾京城內外兵民之用也。

translations.literal: To supply the needs of soldiers and civilians inside and outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: To supply the needs of soldiers and civilians inside and outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 且予不忍山、陝百姓受害，發兵追剿，猶恨未能速定，豈能不愛京城軍民，反行殺戮？

translations.literal: Moreover, I cannot bear to see the people of Shanxi and Shaanxi suffer, and have sent troops in pursuit—yet I regret we have not pacified them more quickly. How then could I fail to care for the army and people of the capital, and instead turn to slaughter?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I cannot bear to see the people of Shanxi and Shaanxi suffer, and have sent troops in pursuit—yet I regret we have not pacified them more quickly. How then could I fail to care for the army and people of the capital, and instead turn to slaughter?

sentences.zh: 此所目擊，何故妄布流言？

translations.literal: These are things you have seen with your own eyes—why spread false rumors?
translations.idiomatic: These are things you have seen with your own eyes—why spread false rumors?

sentences.zh: 是必近京土寇，流賊間諜，有意煽惑搖動，已諭各部嚴捕。

translations.literal: This must be the work of local bandits near the capital and rebel spies, deliberately stirring unrest; I have ordered every department to hunt them down strictly.
translations.idiomatic: This must be the work of local bandits near the capital and rebel spies, deliberately stirring unrest; I have ordered every department to hunt them down strictly.

sentences.zh: 通行曉諭，以安眾心。

translations.literal: [The order] was circulated to reassure the public.
translations.idiomatic: The order was circulated to reassure the public.

sentences.zh: 九月，上入山海關，王率諸王羣臣迎於通州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Emperor entered Shanhaiguan; the Prince led the princes and ministers to welcome him at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Emperor entered Shanhaiguan; the Prince led the princes and ministers to welcome him at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 上至京師，封為叔父攝政王，賜貂蟒朝衣。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached the capital, [the Prince] was created Imperial Uncle Prince Regent and granted a court robe of sable and python-patterned brocade.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor reached the capital, the Prince was created Imperial Uncle Prince Regent and granted a sable-python court robe.

sentences.zh: 十月乙卯朔，上即位，以王功高，命禮部尚書郎球、侍郎藍拜、啟心郎渥赫建碑紀績，加賜冊寶、黑狐冠一、上飾東珠十三、黑狐裘一，副以金、銀、馬、駝。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month the Emperor ascended the throne. Because the Prince's merit was great, he ordered Minister of Rites Lang Qiu, Vice Minister Lan Bai, and Kesinlang Wohe to erect a stele recording his achievements, and additionally bestowed upon him patent and seal, one black-fox crown with thirteen eastern pearls on top, one black-fox fur robe, together with gold, silver, horses, and camels.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the tenth month the Emperor ascended the throne. Because the Prince's merit was great, he ordered Minister of Rites Lang Qiu, Vice Minister Lan Bai, and Kesinlang Wohe to erect a stele recording his achievements, and additionally bestowed patent and seal, a black-fox crown topped with thirteen eastern pearls, a black-fox fur robe, and gold, silver, horses, and camels besides.

sentences.zh: 二年，鄭親王等議上攝政王儀制，視諸王有加禮。

translations.literal: In the second year Prince Zheng and others proposed ceremonial regulations for the Prince Regent, granting him honors beyond those of other princes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Prince Zheng and others proposed ceremonial regulations for the Prince Regent, granting him honors beyond those of other princes.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「上前未敢違禮，他可如議。

translations.literal: The Prince said: "Before the Emperor I dare not transgress protocol; in other matters, your proposal may stand.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince said: "Before the Emperor I dare not transgress protocol; in other matters, your proposal may stand.

sentences.zh: 」翌日入朝，諸臣跪迎，命還輿，責大學士剛林等曰：「此上朝門，諸臣何故跪我？

translations.literal: " The next day he attended court; the ministers knelt to greet him, and he ordered his sedan returned and rebuked Grand Secretaries Ganglin and others, saying: "This is the Emperor's court gate—why do you kneel to me?
translations.idiomatic: " The next day he attended court; the ministers knelt to greet him, and he ordered his sedan returned and rebuked Grand Secretaries Ganglin and others: "This is the Emperor's court gate—why do you kneel to me?

sentences.zh: 」御史趙開心疏言：「王以皇叔之親，兼攝政王之尊，臣民寧肯自外於拜舞？

translations.literal: " Censor Zhao Kaixin submitted a memorial, saying: "The Prince holds the rank of imperial uncle and the dignity of regent—would officials and people willingly stand apart from obeisance?
translations.idiomatic: " Censor Zhao Kaixin submitted a memorial: "The Prince holds the rank of imperial uncle and the dignity of regent—would officials and people willingly stand apart from obeisance?

sentences.zh: 第王恩皆上恩，羣臣謁王，正當限以禮數，與朝見不同。

translations.literal: Yet the Prince's grace is the Emperor's grace; when ministers call upon the Prince, protocol ought to set limits, distinct from an audience with the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Prince's grace is the Emperor's grace; when ministers call upon the Prince, protocol ought to set limits, distinct from an audience with the throne.

sentences.zh: 庶諸臣不失尊王之意，亦全王尊上之心。

translations.literal: Thus ministers would not fail in honoring the Prince, and the Prince would fully preserve his reverence for the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ministers would not fail in honoring the Prince, and the Prince would fully preserve his reverence for the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 上稱叔父攝政王，王為上叔父，惟上得稱之。

translations.literal: The Emperor addresses him as Imperial Uncle Prince Regent; the Prince is the Emperor's imperial uncle—only the Emperor may use that form of address.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor addresses him as Imperial Uncle Prince Regent; the Prince is the Emperor's imperial uncle—only the Emperor may use that form of address.

sentences.zh: 若臣庶宜於叔父上加'皇'字，庶辨上下，尊體制。

translations.literal: For officials and commoners, the word 'Imperial' should be added before 'Uncle,' thus distinguishing superior and subordinate and upholding proper hierarchy.
translations.idiomatic: For officials and commoners, the word 'Imperial' should be added before 'Uncle,' thus distinguishing superior and subordinate and upholding proper hierarchy.

sentences.zh: 」下禮部議行。

translations.literal: " The order was sent down to the Ministry of Rites to deliberate and implement.
translations.idiomatic: " The order was sent down to the Ministry of Rites to deliberate and implement.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，豫親王克揚州，可法死之，遂破明南都。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year Prince Yu captured Yangzhou; Kefa died in its defense, and the southern Ming capital was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year Prince Yu captured Yangzhou; Kefa died in its defense, and the southern Ming capital was then taken.

sentences.zh: 閏六月，英親王逐李自成至武昌，東下九江，故明寧南侯降，江南底定。

translations.literal: In the intercalary sixth month Prince Ying drove Li Zicheng as far as Wuchang, then marched east to Jiujiang; the former Ming Marquis of Pacifying the South surrendered, and the Jiangnan region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary sixth month Prince Ying drove Li Zicheng as far as Wuchang, then marched east to Jiujiang; the former Ming Marquis of Pacifying the South surrendered, and the Jiangnan region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 十月，上賜王馬，王入謝，詔曰：「遇朝賀大典，朕受王禮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Emperor bestowed horses upon the Prince; the Prince entered to give thanks, and an edict said: "At great court ceremonies of congratulation, I shall receive the Prince's salutation.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Emperor bestowed horses upon the Prince; the Prince entered to give thanks, and an edict said: "At great court ceremonies of congratulation, I shall receive the Prince's salutation.

sentences.zh: 若小節，勿與諸王同。

translations.literal: On lesser occasions, do not rank him with the other princes.
translations.idiomatic: On lesser occasions, do not rank him with the other princes.

sentences.zh: 」王對曰：「上方幼衝，臣不敢違禮。

translations.literal: " The Prince replied: "The Emperor is still young; your subject dare not transgress protocol.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince replied: "The Emperor is still young; your subject dare not transgress protocol.

sentences.zh: 待上親政，凡有寵恩，不敢辭。

translations.literal: When the Emperor assumes personal rule, whatever favors and honors there may be, [I] dare not decline.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty comes of age and takes the reins himself, whatever honors you bestow, I will not refuse them.

sentences.zh: 」王時攝政久，位崇功高，時誡諸臣尊事主上，曰：「俟上春秋鼎盛，將歸政焉。

translations.literal: " The Prince had held the regency for a long time; his rank was exalted and his merit great. From time to time he admonished the ministers to respect and serve the sovereign, saying: "When the Emperor reaches the prime of life, I shall return the government to him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince had held the regency for years; his rank was exalted and his achievements unmatched. He repeatedly urged the ministers to honor and serve the sovereign, saying, "When the Emperor reaches his prime, I shall surrender the government to him.

sentences.zh: 初，肅親王怨王不立己，有郄英豫二王與王同母，王視豫親王厚，每寬假之。

translations.literal: At first Prince Su resented that the Prince had not enthroned him. Prince Ying and Prince Yu shared the same mother as the Prince; the Prince favored Prince Yu generously and always treated him leniently.
translations.idiomatic: At first Prince Su resented the Prince for not placing him on the throne. Prince Ying and Prince Yu were his uterine brothers; the Prince favored Prince Yu deeply and always indulged him.

sentences.zh: 豫親王之徵蘇尼特也，王送之出安定門。

translations.literal: When Prince Yu went on campaign against the Sonid, the Prince saw him off as far as Anding Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu marched against the Sonid, the Prince escorted him out through Anding Gate.

sentences.zh: 及歸，迎之烏蘭諾爾。

translations.literal: When he returned, [the Prince] went to meet him at Ulan Nor.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the Prince went to Ulan Nor to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 集諸大臣，語以豫親王功懋，宜封輔政叔王，因罷鄭親王輔政，以授豫親王。

translations.literal: He assembled the grand ministers and told them that Prince Yu's merits were great and that he ought to be enfeoffed as Prince Regent Uncle; thereby he dismissed Prince Zheng from the regency and transferred that authority to Prince Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the grand ministers and declared that Prince Yu's service merited the title Prince Regent Uncle; he then removed Prince Zheng from the regency and gave that office to Prince Yu.

sentences.zh: 肅親王既平四川，王摘其微罪，置之死。

translations.literal: After Prince Su had pacified Sichuan, the Prince seized upon a minor offense and had him put to death.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Su had pacified Sichuan, the Prince seized on a minor offense and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月，王以風疾不勝跪拜，從諸王大臣議，獨賀正旦上前行禮，他悉免。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, the Prince suffered from wind ailment and could not bear kneeling and bowing; following deliberation by the princes and ministers, he alone performed the New Year's greeting before the Emperor; all other ceremonies were waived.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year the Prince was stricken with paralysis and could no longer kneel and bow. At the princes' and ministers' urging he alone offered New Year's greetings before the Emperor; all other rites were excused.

sentences.zh: 五年十一月，南郊禮成，赦詔曰：「叔父攝政王治安天下，有大勳勞，宜加殊禮，以崇功德，尊為皇父攝政王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifth year, after the southern suburban rites were completed, an amnesty edict proclaimed: "The Imperial Uncle Prince Regent has brought peace to all under Heaven and rendered great meritorious service; extraordinary honors ought to be added to exalt his merit and virtue—let him be honored as Imperial Father Prince Regent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fifth year, after the southern suburban sacrifice, an amnesty edict declared: "The Imperial Uncle Prince Regent has brought order to the realm and rendered incomparable service. Extraordinary honors are due to exalt his merit—let him be styled Imperial Father Prince Regent.

sentences.zh: 凡詔疏皆書之。

translations.literal: All edicts and memorials shall bear this title.
translations.idiomatic: All edicts and memorials shall bear this title.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，自將討大同叛將姜瓖，拔渾源。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year, he personally led a campaign against the rebel general Jiang Xiang of Datong and took Hunyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year he took the field in person against Jiang Xiang, the rebel commander at Datong, and captured Hunyuan.

sentences.zh: 聞豫親王病痘，先歸。

translations.literal: On hearing that Prince Yu had fallen ill with smallpox, he returned ahead [of the army].
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Prince Yu had taken ill with smallpox, he hurried back ahead of the army.

sentences.zh: 諭瓖降，未下。

translations.literal: He summoned Jiang Xiang to surrender, but [Datong] was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: He called on Jiang Xiang to surrender, but Datong did not fall.

sentences.zh: 以師行在外，鑄行在印。

translations.literal: Because the army was campaigning in the field, he cast an imperial seal for use on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Because the army was in the field, he had a traveling imperial seal cast.

sentences.zh: 禁諸王及內大臣干預部院政事及漢官升降，不論所言是非，皆治罪。

translations.literal: He forbade princes and inner ministers from interfering in the affairs of the ministries and boards or in the promotion and demotion of Han officials; regardless of whether their words were right or wrong, all were punished.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade princes and inner ministers to meddle in the ministries or in the appointment and dismissal of Han officials; whether their advice was sound or not, all offenders were punished.

sentences.zh: 七月，复徵大同，瓖將楊振威斬瓖降。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, he again marched against Datong; Jiang Xiang's general Yang Zhenwei beheaded Jiang and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he marched on Datong again; Jiang Xiang's general Yang Zhenwei killed Jiang and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十月，移師討喀爾喀二楚呼爾，徵敖漢、扎嚕特、察哈爾、烏喇特、土默特、四子部落以兵來會。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he shifted his army to attack the Khalkha Erchughur; he summoned Ao Han, Jalut, Chakhar, Urat, Tumet, and the Four Ordos tribes to bring troops and join him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he turned his army against the Khalkha chief Erchughur and called up the Ao Han, Jalut, Chakhar, Urat, Tumet, and Four Ordos tribes to join him with their forces.

sentences.zh: 至喀屯布拉克，不見敵，乃還。

translations.literal: Reaching Ketun Bulag, he found no enemy and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Ketun Bulag, found no enemy, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十二月，王妃博爾濟吉特氏薨，以冊寶追封為敬孝忠恭正宮元妃。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Prince's consort of the Borjigit clan died; by patent and seal she was posthumously enfeoffed as Primary Consort of the Inner Palace, honored as Jingxiao Zhonggong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Prince's Borjigit consort died; by patent and seal she was posthumously created Primary Consort of the Inner Palace with the honorific Jingxiao Zhonggong.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，王納肅王福金，福金，妃女弟也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, the Prince took in Fujin, Prince Su's [former] consort; Fujin was the younger sister of [the Prince's deceased] consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year the Prince took Fujin, Prince Su's former consort—she was the younger sister of his own late consort.

sentences.zh: 复徵女朝鮮。

translations.literal: He again solicited a bride from Korea.
translations.idiomatic: He again demanded a bride from Korea.

sentences.zh: 令部事不須題奏者，付巽親王滿達海、端重親王博洛、敬謹親王尼堪料理。

translations.literal: Matters of the ministries not requiring memorial submission he entrusted to Prince Xun Mandahai, Prince Duanshong Boluo, and Prince Jingjin Nikan to handle.
translations.idiomatic: Routine ministry business not requiring memorials to the throne he delegated to Prince Xun Mandahai, Prince Duanshong Boluo, and Prince Jingjin Nikan.

sentences.zh: 五月，率諸王貝勒獵於山海關，朝鮮送女至，王迎於連山，成婚。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, he led the princes and beile on a hunt at Shanhaiguan; when Korea sent the bride, the Prince received her at Lianshan and the marriage was concluded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he led the princes and beile on a hunt at Shanhaiguan; when Korea delivered the bride, the Prince received her at Lianshan and the marriage was celebrated.

sentences.zh: 复獵於中後所，責隨獵王貝勒行列不整，罰鍰有差。

translations.literal: He hunted again at Zhonghousuo, rebuked the princes and beile who accompanied the hunt for disorderly formation, and fined them in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted again at Zhonghousuo, rebuked the princes and beile for falling out of formation, and imposed fines in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 七月，諭以京城當夏溽暑不可堪，擇地築城避暑。
