translations.literal: In the seventh month, he proclaimed that the capital in summer's sweltering heat was unbearable, and that a site should be chosen to build a city for escaping the heat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he announced that the capital's summer heat was unbearable and ordered a site chosen for building a retreat city.

sentences.zh: 令戶部加派直隸、山西、浙江、山東、江南、河南、湖廣、江西、陝西九省地丁銀二百四十九萬兩有奇，輸京師備工用。

translations.literal: He ordered the Ministry of Revenue to levy an additional land-and-poll tax of more than 2.49 million taels of silver across the nine provinces of Zhili, Shanxi, Zhejiang, Shandong, Jiangnan, Henan, Huguang, Jiangxi, and Shaanxi, to be transported to the capital for construction expenses.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Ministry of Revenue to levy an additional land-and-poll tax of more than 2.49 million taels of silver across Zhili, Shanxi, Zhejiang, Shandong, Jiangnan, Henan, Huguang, Jiangxi, and Shaanxi, to be sent to the capital for the building works.

sentences.zh: 八月，王尊所生母太祖妃烏喇納拉氏為孝烈恭敏獻哲仁和讚天儷聖武皇后，祔太廟。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Prince honored his biological mother, Taizu consort Ulanara, as Empress Xiaolie Gongmin Xianzhe Renhe Zantian Lisheng Wu, and enshrined her in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Prince elevated his birth mother, Taizu consort Ulanara, to Empress Xiaolie Gongmin Xianzhe Renhe Zantian Lisheng Wu and had her enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 尋有疾，語貝子錫翰、內大臣席訥布庫等曰：「予罹此大戚，體復不快。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he fell ill and said to Beizi Xihan, inner minister Shenebu, and others: "I have suffered this great grief, and my body is again unwell.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he fell ill and said to Beizi Xihan, inner minister Shenebu, and the others: "I have suffered this great bereavement, and my health has again failed.

sentences.zh: 上雖人主，獨不能循家人禮一臨幸乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor though sovereign—is he alone unable to come once in the manner of family courtesy?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor is sovereign—can he not come even once in the manner of family courtesy?

sentences.zh: 謂上幼衝，爾等皆親近大臣也。

translations.literal: Considering the Emperor's youth, you are all his closest ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor is still young—you are all his closest ministers.

sentences.zh: 」既又戒曰：「毋以予言請上臨幸。

translations.literal: " He then again cautioned them: "Do not use my words to request that the Emperor come to visit.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he added a warning: "Do not use my words to ask the Emperor to visit.

sentences.zh: 」錫翰等出，追止之，不及，上幸王第。

translations.literal: " When Xihan and the others went out, [someone] pursued them to stop them but could not overtake them in time; the Emperor visited the Prince's residence.
translations.idiomatic: " Xihan and the others had barely left when someone ran after them to stop them—but too late; the Emperor had already come to the Prince's residence.

sentences.zh: 王因責錫翰等，議罪當死，旋命貰之。

translations.literal: The Prince thereupon rebuked Xihan and the others; on deliberation their offense merited death, but soon he ordered their lives spared.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince rebuked Xihan and the others; on deliberation their offense merited death, but he soon pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 十一月，复獵於邊外。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he hunted again beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he hunted again beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 十二月，薨於喀喇城，年三十九。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, he died at Kala City at the age of thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he died at Kala City, aged thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，震悼。

translations.literal: The Emperor, on hearing of it, was shaken with grief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard the news, he was stricken with grief.

sentences.zh: 喪還，率王大臣縞服迎奠東直門外。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned, he led princes and ministers in unhemmed hemp mourning to receive and mourn [the Prince] outside Dongzhi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin returned, he led princes and ministers in unhemmed hemp mourning to receive and mourn the Prince outside Dongzhi Gate.

sentences.zh: 詔追尊為懋德修道廣業定功安民立政誠敬義皇帝，廟號成宗。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously honored him as Emperor with the title Maode Xiudao Guangye Dinggong Anmin Lizheng Chengjing Yi, temple name Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously honored him as Emperor Maode Xiudao Guangye Dinggong Anmin Lizheng Chengjing Yi, with the temple name Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，尊妃為義皇后。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, his consort was honored as Empress Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year his consort was honored as Empress Yi.

sentences.zh: 祔太廟。

translations.literal: She was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: She was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 王無子，以豫親王子多爾博為後，襲親王，俸視諸王三倍，詔留護近侍蘇克薩哈、詹岱為議政大臣。

translations.literal: The Prince had no sons; Prince Yu's son Dorgobo was adopted as his heir, inherited the princedom, and received stipend at triple that of other princes. An edict retained the close attendants Suksaha and Zhandai as deliberative ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince had no sons; Prince Yu's son Dorgobo was adopted as his heir, inherited the princedom, and received triple the stipend of other princes. An edict retained his close attendants Suksaha and Zhandai as deliberative ministers.

sentences.zh: 二月，蘇克薩哈、詹岱訐告王薨時，其侍女吳爾庫尼將殉，請以王所製八補黃袍、大東珠素珠、黑貂褂置棺內。

translations.literal: In the second month, Suksaha and Zhandai denounced [him, reporting that] at the Prince's death his maidservant Wu'erkuni was about to follow him in death and had requested that the eight-panel yellow robe, large plain eastern pearl, and black sable jacket made by the Prince be placed in the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Suksaha and Zhandai accused him, reporting that at his death the maidservant Wu'erkuni was about to follow him in death and had asked that an eight-panel yellow robe, a large plain eastern pearl, and a black sable jacket of the Prince's making be placed in the coffin.

sentences.zh: 王在時，欲以兩固山駐永平，謀篡大位。

translations.literal: While the Prince lived, he had wished to station two banners at Yongping and plotted to seize the supreme throne.
translations.idiomatic: While he lived, the Prince had planned to station two banners at Yongping and seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 固山額真譚泰亦言王納肅王福金，復令肅王子至第較射，何洛會以惡言詈之。

translations.literal: The banners ejen Tan Tai also testified that the Prince had taken Prince Su's consort Fujin, again summoned Prince Su's son to his residence for an archery contest, and that Heluen had reviled [the son] with foul words.
translations.idiomatic: The banners ejen Tan Tai also testified that the Prince had taken Prince Su's consort Fujin, summoned Prince Su's son to his residence for an archery contest, and that Heluen had reviled the boy with foul abuse.

sentences.zh: 於是鄭親王濟爾哈朗、巽親王滿達海、端重親王博洛、敬謹親王尼堪及內大臣等疏言：「昔太宗文皇帝龍馭上賓，諸王大臣共矢忠誠，翊戴皇上。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince Zheng Jirhalang, Prince Xun Mandahai, Prince Duanshong Boluo, Prince Jingjin Nikan, and the inner ministers submitted a memorial, saying: "Formerly, when the Taizong Emperor Wen ascended to the Highest Guest, the princes and ministers together pledged loyalty and supported the enthronement of the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Prince Zheng Jirhalang, Prince Xun Mandahai, Prince Duanshong Boluo, Prince Jingjin Nikan, and the inner ministers submitted a memorial: "When the Taizong Emperor Wen departed this life, the princes and ministers pledged their loyalty and raised the Emperor to the throne.

sentences.zh: 方在衝年，令臣濟爾哈朗與睿親王多爾袞同輔政。

translations.literal: The Emperor was still in minority; we were ordered that your subject Jirhalang and Prince Rui Dorgon should jointly assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was still a child; your subject Jirhalang and Prince Rui Dorgon were ordered to govern jointly as regents.

sentences.zh: 逮後多爾袞獨擅威權，不令濟爾哈朗預政，遂以母弟多鐸為輔政叔王。

translations.literal: Later Dorgon monopolized authority alone, would not permit Jirhalang to participate in government, and then installed his uterine brother Dodo as Prince Regent Uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Later Dorgon seized power for himself, barred Jirhalang from government, and installed his uterine brother Dodo as Prince Regent Uncle.

sentences.zh: 背誓肆行，妄自尊大，自稱皇父攝政王。

translations.literal: He broke his oath and acted wantonly, arrogantly exalted himself, and styled himself Imperial Father Prince Regent.
translations.idiomatic: He broke his oath and acted with impunity, arrogantly exalted himself, and styled himself Imperial Father Prince Regent.

sentences.zh: 凡批票本章，一以皇父攝政王行之。

translations.literal: For all endorsements on memorial submissions, he carried them out entirely in the name of the Imperial Father Regent.
translations.idiomatic: Every endorsement on submitted memorials was issued solely as the Imperial Father Regent.

sentences.zh: 儀仗、音樂、侍從、府第，僭擬至尊。

translations.literal: Guard of honor, music, attendants, and residence—all presumptuously imitated the supreme sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: His guard of honor, court music, retinue, and mansion all aped those reserved for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 擅稱太宗文皇帝序不當立，以挾制皇上。

translations.literal: He arbitrarily claimed that Emperor Wen Taizong's succession had been improperly established, thereby coercing the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He presumed to declare Taizong's succession illegitimate, using this claim to hold the emperor hostage.

sentences.zh: 構陷威逼，使肅親王不得其死，遂納其妃，且收其財產。

translations.literal: Through framed charges and coercion he caused Prince Su to die unjustly, then took Prince Su's consort and seized his property.
translations.idiomatic: By fabricated accusations and intimidation he drove Prince Su to an unjust death, took the prince's consort for himself, and confiscated his estate.

sentences.zh: 更悖理入生母於太廟。

translations.literal: Further, in violation of principle, he installed his birth mother in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He went further still, in brazen defiance of propriety, by enshrining his own mother in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 僭妄不可枚舉。

translations.literal: His presumptuous excesses cannot be enumerated.
translations.idiomatic: His usurpations and arrogance are too numerous to list.

sentences.zh: 臣等從前畏威吞聲，今冒死奏聞，伏原重加處治。

translations.literal: We your ministers formerly feared his power and swallowed our voices; now we risk death to report this, humbly begging severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: We once feared his power and kept silent; now we risk our lives to bring this before Your Majesty and humbly pray that he receive the full weight of punishment.

sentences.zh: 」詔削爵，撤廟享，並罷孝烈武皇后諡號廟享，黜宗室，籍財產入官，多爾博歸宗。

translations.literal: " An edict stripped his nobility, removed temple sacrifices, and also abolished Empress Xiaoliewu's posthumous title and temple sacrifices; he was expelled from the imperial clan, his property was registered and confiscated for the state, and Dorbod was returned to his original clan.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict then stripped him of his rank, ended his temple rites, and revoked Empress Xiaoliewu's posthumous honors and temple sacrifices as well. He was cast out of the imperial clan, his property was seized for the treasury, and Dorbod was restored to his birth lineage.

sentences.zh: 十二年，吏科副理事官彭長庚、一等精奇尼哈番許爾安各疏頌王功，請復爵號，下王大臣議，長庚、爾安坐論死，詔流寧古塔。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Associate Deputy Director of the Office of Personnel Review Peng Changgeng and first-class jingqi niha fan Xu Er'an each submitted memorials praising the prince's merits and requesting restoration of his titles. The matter was referred to the princes and grand ministers for deliberation. Changgeng and Er'an were found guilty and sentenced to death; an edict commuted this to exile at Ningguta.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, Peng Changgeng, associate deputy director in the Office of Personnel Review, and Xu Er'an, a first-class jingqi niha fan, each submitted memorials praising the prince's service and asking that his titles be restored. The case was sent to the princes and grand ministers for review. Changgeng and Er'an were condemned to death, but an edict sent them into exile at Ningguta instead.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十八年，高宗詔曰：「睿親王多爾袞攝政有年，威福自專，歿後其屬人首告，入關，肅清京輦，檄定中原，前勞未可盡泯。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Qianlong, the Gaozong Emperor issued an edict: "Prince Rui Dorgon held the regency for many years and wielded power for himself alone; after his death his subordinates made accusations against him. Yet in crossing the frontier, securing the capital, and pacifying the Central Plain by proclamation, his earlier service cannot be entirely effaced.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 38, the Qianlong Emperor issued an edict: "Prince Rui Dorgon had held the regency for years and kept power to himself; after his death his own followers turned accuser. Yet in entering the pass, clearing the capital, and proclaiming order across the Central Plain, his earlier achievements cannot be wholly forgotten.

sentences.zh: 今其後嗣？

translations.literal: As for his descendants today?
translations.idiomatic: As for his descendants today?

sentences.zh: 定罪除封。

translations.literal: They were found guilty and stripped of their enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: They were convicted and stripped of their titles.

sentences.zh: 第念定鼎之初，王實統廢絕，塋域榛蕪，殊堪憫惻。

translations.literal: Yet considering that at the founding of the dynasty the prince's line was truly cut off, and his tomb lies overgrown and neglected—a matter truly deserving compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at the dynasty's founding his line was truly extinguished, and his grave now lies overgrown and forsaken—a sight that moves one to pity.

sentences.zh: 交內務府派員繕葺，並令近支王公以時祭掃。

translations.literal: Let the Imperial Household Department assign officials to repair it, and order closely related princes and dukes to perform seasonal sacrifices and maintenance.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Household Department shall send officials to restore the tomb, and closely related princes and dukes shall tend it with seasonal offerings.

sentences.zh: 」四十三年正月，又詔曰：「睿親王多爾袞掃蕩賊氛，肅清宮禁。

translations.literal: " In the first month of the forty-third year, another edict said: "Prince Rui Dorgon swept away the bandit menace and secured the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: " In the first month of the forty-third year, another edict declared: "Prince Rui Dorgon cleared away the rebel threat and secured the palace.

sentences.zh: 分遣諸王，追殲流寇，撫定疆陲。

translations.literal: He dispatched the princes in separate columns to pursue and destroy the roving bandits and pacify the frontier regions.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the princes in separate forces to hunt down the roving rebels and pacify the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 創制規模，皆所經畫。

translations.literal: The founding institutions and framework were all of his planning.
translations.idiomatic: The institutions and framework of the new order were largely of his design.

sentences.zh: 尋奉世祖車駕入都，成一統之業，厥功最著。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he escorted the Shizu Emperor's imperial carriage into the capital, completing the work of unification—his merit was the most outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: He then escorted the Shunzhi Emperor into the capital and brought the work of unification to completion; among all contributors, his service stood foremost.

sentences.zh: 歿後為蘇克薩哈所構，首告誣以謀逆。

translations.literal: After his death he was framed by Suksaha, whose initial accusation slandered him with plotting treason.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Suksaha framed him, lodging a first accusation that falsely charged him with treason.

sentences.zh: 其時世祖尚在衝齡，未嘗親政，經諸王定罪除封。

translations.literal: At that time Shizu was still in his tender years and had not yet personally ruled; the princes found him guilty and stripped his enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: The Shunzhi Emperor was still a child and had not yet taken power in his own right; the princes convicted Dorgon and stripped his titles.

sentences.zh: 朕念王果萌異志，兵權在握，何事不可為？

translations.literal: I reflect: if the prince truly harbored rebellious intent, with military power in his grasp, what could he not have done?
translations.idiomatic: I ask myself: if the prince truly nursed rebellious designs, with the army in his hand, what could he not have done?

sentences.zh: 乃不於彼時因利乘便，直至身後始以斂服僭用龍袞，證為覬覦，有是理乎？

translations.literal: Yet he did not seize the opportunity then and take advantage of circumstances; only after his death was it alleged, on the basis of his burial garments and presumptuous use of the dragon robe, that he had coveted the throne—is such a thing reasonable?
translations.idiomatic: Why did he not seize the moment when he held every advantage, only to be accused after death of coveting the throne because his burial garments presumptuously bore the dragon robe—is that credible?

sentences.zh: 實錄載：'王集諸王大臣，遣人傳語曰：「今觀諸王大臣但知媚予，鮮能尊上，予豈能容此？

translations.literal: The Veritable Records state: 'The prince assembled the princes and grand ministers and sent someone to relay these words: "Looking at you princes and ministers today, I see that you know only how to flatter me and scarcely how to honor the sovereign—how can I tolerate this?
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records record: 'The prince summoned the princes and grand ministers and sent word: "I see among you only flattery toward me and little respect for the sovereign—how can I abide this?

sentences.zh: 昔太宗升遐，嗣君未立，英王、豫王跪請予即尊，予曰：'若果如此言，予即當自刎。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended to heaven, the heir had not yet been established; Prince Ying and Prince Yu knelt and begged me to take the supreme throne at once. I said, 'If you truly mean such words, I shall cut my own throat on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong passed away and no heir had yet been named, Prince Ying and Prince Yu knelt and begged me to take the throne myself. I said, 'If you truly mean that, I shall cut my own throat here and now.

sentences.zh: 』誓死不從，遂奉今上即位。

translations.literal: ' Swearing he would rather die than comply, he then installed the present sovereign on the throne.
translations.idiomatic: ' Swearing he would rather die than accept, he then installed the present emperor on the throne.

sentences.zh: 似此危疑之日，以予為君，予尚不可；

translations.literal: On such a day of crisis and doubt, to make me sovereign—even that I would not accept;
translations.idiomatic: On a day so perilous and uncertain, even making me sovereign I would not accept;

sentences.zh: 今乃不敬上而媚予，予何能容？

translations.literal: and now you show no respect for the sovereign but flatter me—how can I tolerate this?
translations.idiomatic: and now you withhold respect from the sovereign and fawn on me instead—how can I tolerate it?

sentences.zh: 自今後有忠於上者，予用之愛之；

translations.literal: From this day forward, whoever is loyal to the sovereign—I shall employ and cherish him;
translations.idiomatic: From this day on, whoever is loyal to the sovereign I shall employ and favor;

sentences.zh: 其不忠於上者，雖媚予，予不爾宥。

translations.literal: whoever is disloyal to the sovereign, though he may flatter me, I shall not pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: whoever is disloyal to the sovereign, though he flatters me, I shall not pardon.

sentences.zh: 」且云：「太宗恩育予躬，所以特異於諸子弟者，蓋深信諸子弟之成立，惟予能成立之。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Taizong nurtured me with grace; the reason he treated me differently from his other sons was that he deeply trusted that among all his sons, only I could bring them to maturity.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said: "Taizong raised me with special favor; the reason he singled me out among his sons was his deep trust that only I could see them all safely established.

sentences.zh: 」'朕每覽實錄至此，未嘗不為之墮淚。

translations.literal: " ' Whenever I read the Veritable Records to this point, I never fail to be moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: " ' Whenever I read the Veritable Records to this passage, I am always moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 則王之立心行事，實為篤忠藎，感厚恩，明君臣大義。

translations.literal: Thus the prince's intentions and conduct were truly steeped in loyal devotion—grateful for great favor, and clear on the great principle between monarch and subject.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's heart and actions were truly steeped in loyal devotion—grateful for great favor and clear on the bond between sovereign and subject.

sentences.zh: 乃由宵小奸謀，構成？

translations.literal: Yet it was the treacherous design of petty villains that fabricated—
translations.idiomatic: Yet petty villains' treachery fabricated—

sentences.zh: 獄，豈可不為之昭雪？

translations.literal: a treason case—can this not be cleared?
translations.idiomatic: a treason case—how can his name not be cleared?

sentences.zh: 宜復還睿親王封號，追諡曰忠，配享太廟。

translations.literal: His Prince Rui title should be restored, he should be posthumously honored with the epithet Loyal, and granted sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: His Prince Rui title should be restored, he should receive the posthumous epithet Loyal, and be granted a place in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 依親王園寢制，修其塋墓，令太常寺春秋致祭。

translations.literal: Following the regulations for princely garden tombs, repair his grave; order the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to perform spring and autumn offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Following the regulations for princely garden tombs, his grave shall be restored, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices shall offer spring and autumn sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 其爵世襲罔替。

translations.literal: His title shall be hereditary in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: The title shall pass in perpetuity from heir to heir.

sentences.zh: 多爾博歸宗封貝勒，命仍還為王后，以其五世孫輔國公淳穎襲爵。

translations.literal: Dorbod had been returned to his original clan and enfeoffed as a beile; [the court] ordered the Prince Rui title restored, and his fifth-generation descendant, Defender of the State Duke Chunying, inherited the rank.
translations.idiomatic: Dorbod, who had been returned to his birth lineage and enfeoffed as a beile, was now ordered restored to the Prince Rui title; his fifth-generation descendant, Defender of the State Duke Chunying, inherited the rank.

sentences.zh: 四世祖鎮國公蘇爾發、曾祖輔國公塞勒、祖輔國恪勤公功宜布先已進封信郡王，至是與淳穎父信恪郡王如松並追封睿親王。

translations.literal: The fourth-generation ancestor, Defender of the Realm Duke Su'erfa; the great-grandfather, Defender of the State Duke Saile; and the grandfather, Defender of the State Duke Gong Yibu the Diligent—all had previously been advanced to Prince of the Second Rank Xinjun. At this time, together with Chunying's father, Prince of the Second Rank Rusong the Trustworthy and Respectful, they were posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Chunying's fourth-generation ancestor Su'erfa, Defender of the Realm Duke; his great-grandfather Saile, Defender of the State Duke; and his grandfather Gong Yibu, Defender of the State Duke the Diligent—all had earlier been promoted to Prince Xinjun. Now, together with Chunying's father Rusong, Prince of the Second Rank the Trustworthy and Respectful, they were posthumously created Prince Rui.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，淳穎薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing, Chunying died.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 5, Chunying died.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously titled Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posthumous epithet Respectful.

sentences.zh: 子寶恩，襲。

translations.literal: His son Bao'en succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bao'en inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，薨，諡曰慎。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year, [he] died; posthumous title: Cautious.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year he died and received the posthumous epithet Cautious.

sentences.zh: 弟瑞恩，襲。

translations.literal: His younger brother Rui'en succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Rui'en inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 道光六年，薨，諡曰勤。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang, [he] died; posthumous title: Diligent.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 6 he died and received the posthumous epithet Diligent.

sentences.zh: 子仁壽，襲。

translations.literal: His son Renshou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Renshou inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 道光九年，上巡盛京謁陵，追念忠王，推恩賜三眼花翎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang, when the emperor toured Shengjing to pay respects at the tombs, remembering the Loyal Prince, he extended favor and granted the three-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 9, when the emperor toured Shengjing to visit the tombs, he remembered the Loyal Prince and, as a mark of grace, bestowed the three-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，薨，諡曰僖。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi, [he] died; posthumous title: Merry.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 3 he died and received the posthumous epithet Merry.

sentences.zh: 子德長，襲。

translations.literal: His son Dechang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dechang inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，薨，諡曰愨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu, [he] died; posthumous title: Sincere.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 2 he died and received the posthumous epithet Sincere.

sentences.zh: 子魁斌，襲。

translations.literal: His son Kuibin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuibin inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 豫通親王多鐸，太祖第十五子。

translations.literal: Prince Yu the Penetrating, Dodo, was the fifteenth son of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Dodo, Prince Yu the Penetrating, was the fifteenth son of Taizu.

sentences.zh: 初封貝勒。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as beile.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as a beile.

sentences.zh: 天聰二年，從太宗伐多羅特部有功，賜號額爾克楚呼爾。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancong, he followed Taizong in attacking the Dorot tribe and had merit; he was granted the title Erke Chuhor.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 2 (1628), he followed Hong Taiji against the Dorot and was rewarded with the honorific Erke Chuhor for his service.

sentences.zh: 三年，從上伐明，自龍井關入，偕莽古爾泰、多爾袞以偏師降漢兒莊城。

translations.literal: In the third year, he followed the sovereign in campaigning against Ming, entered through Longjing Pass, and together with Manggu'ertai and Dorgon, with a detached column, induced the surrender of Han'erzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he marched against Ming with the khan, entered through Longjing Pass, and with Manggu'ertai and Dorgon led a flanking force that brought Han'erzhuang to surrender.

sentences.zh: 會大軍克遵化，薄明都。

translations.literal: When the main army captured Zunhua, [they] pressed close to the Ming capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army took Zunhua, the invasion force drew close to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 廣渠門之役，多鐸以幼留後，明潰兵來犯，擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the Battle of Guangqu Gate, Dodo, being young, was left behind; routed Ming troops came to attack, and he drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Guangqu Gate, the young Dodo was left in the rear. When routed Ming troops attacked, he beat them back.

sentences.zh: 師還，次薊州，复擊破明援兵。

translations.literal: When the army returned and halted at Jizhou, he again defeated Ming relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march, the army stopped at Jizhou, where he again routed Ming reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 五年，從圍大凌河城，為正白旗後應，克近城台堡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he followed in besieging Daling River city, serving as rear support for the Plain White Banner, and captured the nearby walled tower forts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he joined the siege of Daling River, acting as rearguard for the Plain White Banner and taking the outlying tower forts.

sentences.zh: 明兵出錦州，屯小凌河岸，上率二百騎馳擊，明兵走。

translations.literal: Ming troops came out from Jinzhou and encamped on the banks of the Xiao Ling River; the sovereign led two hundred cavalry in a swift attack, and the Ming troops fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ming troops sallied from Jinzhou and encamped on the Xiao Ling River. The khan led two hundred horsemen in a dash against them and put them to flight.

sentences.zh: 多鐸逐之，薄錦州，墜馬，馬逸入敵陣，乃奪軍校馬乘以還。

translations.literal: Dodo pursued them, pressing close to Jinzhou; he fell from his horse, which bolted into the enemy ranks, so he seized a military officer's horse and rode back.
translations.idiomatic: Dodo pursued them to the walls of Jinzhou. He was thrown from his horse when it bolted into the enemy lines, but seized a commander's mount and fought his way back.

sentences.zh: 六年，從伐察哈爾，將右翼兵，俘其眾千餘

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he followed in attacking the Chakhar, commanded the right-wing troops, and captured more than a thousand of their people.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he campaigned against the Chakhar at the head of the right wing and took more than a thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔問徵明及朝鮮、察哈爾三者何先，多鐸言：「我軍非怯於戰，豈可必得？

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict asked which of attacking Ming, Korea, or the Chakhar should come first; Dodo said: "Our army is not cowardly in battle—how can victory be assured?
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year an edict asked whether Ming, Korea, or the Chakhar should be attacked first. Dodo replied: "Our army is not afraid to fight—yet how can we be sure of victory?

sentences.zh: 夫攻山海關與攻燕京，等攻耳。

translations.literal: Attacking Shanhaiguan and attacking Yanjing are the same sort of attack.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking Shanhaiguan and attacking Yanjing are one and the same.

sentences.zh: 臣以為宜直入關，庶饜士卒望，亦久遠計也。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that we ought to enter the pass directly, so as to satisfy the soldiers' hopes and also as a long-range plan.
translations.idiomatic: I believe we should drive straight through the pass to satisfy the troops' longing for victory and to serve our long-term interests.

sentences.zh: 且相機審時，古今同然。

translations.literal: Moreover, sizing up the moment and gauging the times—this has been the same in every age.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing the opportune moment has always been the rule, past and present alike.

sentences.zh: 我軍若弛而敵有備，何隙之可乘？

translations.literal: If our army relaxes while the enemy is prepared, what opening can we exploit?
translations.idiomatic: If we slacken while the enemy stands ready, what opening will there be for us to exploit?

sentences.zh: 吾何愛於明而必言和？

translations.literal: Why should I cherish Ming and insist on speaking of peace?
translations.idiomatic: Why should I be fond of Ming and insist on talking peace?

sentences.zh: 亦念士卒勞苦，姑為委蛇。

translations.literal: I also bear in mind the soldiers' toil and hardship, and for the moment practice evasion.
translations.idiomatic: I only consider the soldiers' hardship and therefore temporize for now.

sentences.zh: 倘時可乘，何待再計。

translations.literal: If the time can be seized, why wait to reconsider?
translations.idiomatic: When the moment is ripe, why hesitate to act?

sentences.zh: 至察哈爾，且勿加兵；

translations.literal: As for the Chakhar, for the time being do not send troops against them;
translations.idiomatic: As for the Chakhar, do not commit troops against them for now;

sentences.zh: 朝鮮已和，亦勿遽絕。

translations.literal: Korea has already made peace—do not break it off hastily either.
translations.idiomatic: Korea is already at peace with us—do not cut off relations rashly.

sentences.zh: 當先圖其大者。

translations.literal: We should first aim at the greater matter.
translations.idiomatic: We should strike first at the main prize.

sentences.zh: 八年，從上略宣府，自巴顏珠爾克進。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he followed the sovereign in raiding Xuanfu, advancing from Bayanzhu'erke.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he joined the khan in raiding Xuanfu, advancing from Bayanzhu'erke.

sentences.zh: 尋攻龍門，未下，趨保安，克之。

translations.literal: Soon he attacked Longmen; it was not taken, so he hurried to Bao'an and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked Longmen but failed to take it, turned toward Bao'an, and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 謁上應州。

translations.literal: He paid respects to the sovereign at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to the khan at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 复略朔州，經五台山，還。

translations.literal: He again raided Shuozhou, passed through Wutai Mountain, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He raided Shuozhou again, marched through the Wutai Mountains, and returned.

sentences.zh: 敗明兵大同。

translations.literal: He defeated Ming troops at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He routed Ming forces at Datong.

sentences.zh: 九年，上遣諸貝勒伐明，徇山西，命多鐸率師入寧、錦綴明師。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the sovereign dispatched the beiles to campaign against Ming and sweep through Shanxi; he ordered Dodo to lead troops into Ning and Jin to pin down Ming forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the khan sent the beiles against Ming to sweep Shanxi and ordered Dodo to march into Ning and Jin to tie down Ming reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 遂自廣寧入，遣固山額真阿山、石廷柱率兵四百前驅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he entered from Guangning, dispatching the banners ejen Ashan and Shi Tingzhu to lead four hundred men as advance guard.
translations.idiomatic: He entered from Guangning and sent the banners ejen Ashan and Shi Tingzhu ahead with four hundred men.

sentences.zh: 祖大壽合錦州、松山兵三千五百屯大凌河西，多鐸率所部馳擊之，大壽兵潰。

translations.literal: Zu Dashou combined three thousand five hundred troops from Jinzhou and Songshan and encamped west of the Daling River; Dodo led his own troops in a swift attack, and Zu Dashou's army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Dashou mustered thirty-five hundred men from Jinzhou and Songshan and encamped west of the Daling River. Dodo charged with his division and smashed Zu Dashou's force.

sentences.zh: 命分道追擊，一至錦州，一至松山，斬獲無算。

translations.literal: He ordered pursuit along separate routes—one column to Jinzhou, one to Songshan—with incalculable kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: He split his forces in pursuit—one column toward Jinzhou, one toward Songshan—inflicting countless casualties and captures.

sentences.zh: 翌日，克台一，還駐廣寧。

translations.literal: The next day he captured one tower fort and returned to encamp at Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he took one tower fort and withdrew to Guangning.

sentences.zh: 師還，上出懷遠門五里迎勞，賜良馬五、甲五。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the sovereign came out five li beyond Huaiyuan Gate to welcome and reward them, granting five fine horses and five suits of armor.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return the khan rode out five li beyond Huaiyuan Gate to welcome them, bestowing five fine horses and five suits of armor.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之曰：「朕幼弟初專閫，即能制勝，是可嘉也！

translations.literal: The sovereign commended him, saying: "My young brother, on his first sole command, was able to win victory—this is praiseworthy!
translations.idiomatic: The khan praised him: "My young brother, given sole command for the first time, won a clear victory—this is truly admirable!

sentences.zh: 崇德元年四月，封豫親王，掌禮部事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Chongde, he was enfeoffed as Prince Yu and put in charge of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Chongde 1 he was created Prince Yu and given charge of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 從伐朝鮮，自沙河堡領兵千人繼噶布什賢兵，至朝鮮都城。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Korea, leading a thousand men from Shahebao to follow up the Kubushixian troops, and reached the Korean capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the Korean campaign he led a thousand men from Shahebao to reinforce the vanguard column and marched to the Korean capital.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮全羅、忠清二道援兵至南漢山，多鐸擊敗之，收其馬千餘。

translations.literal: Korean relief troops from the Jeolla and Chungcheong circuits reached Nanhansan; Dodo defeated them and seized more than a thousand of their horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Korean reinforcements from Jeolla and Chungcheong reached Nanhansan, Dodo routed them and captured more than a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 揚古利為殘兵所賊，捕得其人，斬以祭。

translations.literal: Yangguli was killed by remnant troops; [Dodo] captured the men responsible and executed them as sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Remnant troops killed Yangguli; Dodo seized the culprits and executed them as blood offerings at his grave.

sentences.zh: 三年，伐錦州，自蒙古扎袞博倫界分率巴牙喇及土默特兵入明境，克大興堡，俘其居民，道遇明諜，擒之。

translations.literal: In the third year, campaigning against Jinzhou, he separately led the Baturu and Tumed troops into Ming territory from the Mongol border at Zhagun Bolun, captured Daxing Fort, took its inhabitants captive, and on the road encountered a Ming spy, whom he seized.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on the Jinzhou campaign, he led the Baturu guard and Tumed troops into Ming territory from the Mongol border at Zhagun Bolun, took Daxing Fort and its people, and captured a Ming spy encountered en route.

sentences.zh: 詔與鄭親王濟爾哈朗軍會，經中後所，大壽以兵來襲，我軍傷九人，亡馬三十。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to join Prince Zheng Jirhalang's army; passing through Zhonghousuo, Zu Dashou attacked with troops; our army had nine wounded and lost thirty horses.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to rendezvous with Prince Zheng Jirhalang, he passed through Zhonghousuo, where Zu Dashou attacked. Nine of his men were wounded and thirty horses lost.

sentences.zh: 多鐸且戰且走，夜達鄭親王所，合師薄中後所城。

translations.literal: Dodo fought while retreating and by night reached Prince Zheng's camp; the united armies pressed close to Zhonghousuo city.
translations.idiomatic: Dodo fought a fighting retreat and by night reached Prince Zheng's camp. The combined forces then advanced on Zhonghousuo.

sentences.zh: 上統師至，敵不敢出。

translations.literal: The sovereign arrived at the head of the army, and the enemy did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: When the khan arrived at the head of the main army, the enemy dared not sally forth.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，上御崇政殿，召多鐸戒諭之，數其罪，下諸王、貝勒、大臣議，削爵，奪所屬入官。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, the sovereign attended at the Chongzheng Hall, summoned Dodo to admonish and instruct him, enumerated his crimes, and referred the matter to the princes, beiles, and ministers for deliberation; his rank was stripped and his holdings confiscated to the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year the khan appeared at the Chongzheng Hall, summoned Dodo to reprimand him, listed his offenses, and referred the case to the princes, beiles, and ministers. His title was stripped and his property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 上命降貝勒，罰銀萬，奪其奴僕、牲畜三之一，予睿親王多爾袞。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered his rank reduced to beile, fined him ten thousand taels of silver, confiscated one third of his slaves, servants, and livestock, and granted them to Prince Rui Dorgon.
translations.idiomatic: The khan demoted him to beile, fined him ten thousand taels, confiscated a third of his slaves, servants, and livestock, and transferred them to Prince Rui Dorgon.

sentences.zh: 尋命掌兵部。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to take charge of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon afterward given charge of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 十月，伐寧遠，擊斬明總兵金國鳳。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, campaigning against Ningyuan, he attacked and killed the Ming commander-in-chief Jin Guofeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he marched on Ningyuan, attacked, and killed the Ming commander Jin Guofeng.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，命與鄭親王濟爾哈朗率師修義州城，駐兵屯田，並擾明山海關外，毋使得耕稼。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, [Dodo] was ordered together with Prince Zheng Jirhalang to lead troops to repair Yizhou city, garrison soldiers for farming colonies, and also harass outside Shanhaiguan so that Ming could not obtain harvests.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year he was ordered to join Prince Zheng Jirhalang in repairing the walls of Yizhou, stationing troops for garrison farming, and raiding beyond Shanhaiguan so the Ming could not bring in their crops.

sentences.zh: 五月，上臨視。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the sovereign came in person to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the khan came in person to inspect the works.

sentences.zh: 附明蒙古多羅特部蘇班岱降，上命偕鄭親王以兵迎之，經錦州杏山，明兵來追，奮擊敗之，賜禦？

translations.literal: Subutai of the Dorot Mongols attached to Ming submitted; the sovereign ordered [Dodo] to join Prince Zheng with troops to receive him. Passing through Xingshan near Jinzhou, Ming troops pursued; [they] fought fiercely and defeated them, and was granted an imperial ?
translations.idiomatic: Subutai of the Dorot Mongols who had been attached to Ming submitted. The khan ordered Dodo to join Prince Zheng with troops to escort him in. Near Xingshan outside Jinzhou, Ming forces gave chase; they fought back fiercely and routed them, earning an imperial reward.

sentences.zh: 良馬一。

translations.literal: One fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: The reward was one fine horse from the imperial stables.

sentences.zh: 圍錦州，夜伏兵桑阿爾齋堡，旦，敵至，敗之，追至塔山，斬八十餘級，獲馬二十。

translations.literal: Besieging Jinzhou, at night [they] hid troops at Sang'arzha Fort; at dawn the enemy arrived, [they] defeated them, pursued to Tashan, beheaded more than eighty, and captured twenty horses.
translations.idiomatic: While investing Jinzhou they hid troops overnight at Sang'arzha Fort. At dawn the enemy came up and was beaten; the pursuit carried to Tashan, where more than eighty heads were taken and twenty horses captured.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，复圍錦州，環城立八營，鑿壕以困之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year, [they] again besieged Jinzhou, set up eight camps around the city, and dug trenches to hem it in.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year they again invested Jinzhou, ringed the city with eight camps, and dug trenches to starve it out.

sentences.zh: 大壽城守蒙古將諾木齊約降，師縋以入，擊大壽，挈降者出，置之義州。

translations.literal: Nomochi, the Mongol commander defending the city for Zu Dashou, agreed to surrender; the army let [him] down by rope to enter, attacked Dashou, brought the defector out, and settled him at Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nomochi, a Mongol officer holding the city for Zu Dashou, agreed to defect. Our men lowered him in by rope, struck at Dashou, brought the turncoat out, and resettled him at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 明援兵自杏山至松山，多鐸與鄭親王率兩翼兵伏錦州南山西岡及松山北嶺，縱噶布什賢兵誘敵，夾擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Ming relief troops came from Xingshan to Songshan; Dodo and Prince Zheng led the two wing forces to lie in ambush on the western ridge of the southern hills at Jinzhou and on the northern ridge at Songshan, sent vanguard cavalry to lure the enemy, and attacked from both sides, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Ming reinforcements marched from Xingshan toward Songshan. Dodo and Prince Zheng posted the two wings in ambush on the western spur of Jinzhou's southern hills and on Songshan's northern ridge, sent vanguard cavalry to draw the enemy in, and crushed them in a pincer.

sentences.zh: 洪承疇以十三萬援錦州，上自盛京馳六日抵松山，環城而營，明兵震怖，宵遁。

translations.literal: Hong Chengchou came with one hundred thirty thousand men to relieve Jinzhou; the sovereign galloped from Shenyang and in six days reached Songshan, encamped around the city, and the Ming army was terrified and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chengchou marched to relieve Jinzhou with a hundred and thirty thousand men. The khan rode hard from Shenyang and reached Songshan in six days, encircled the city with camps, and the Ming army broke in terror and fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 多鐸伏兵道旁，明總兵吳三桂、王朴自杏山奔寧遠，我軍追及於高橋，伏發，三桂等僅以身免。

translations.literal: Dodo lay in ambush by the road; Ming regional commanders Wu Sangui and Wang Pu fled from Xingshan toward Ningyuan; our army overtook them at Gaoqiao, the ambush sprang, and Sangui and the others barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Dodo hid troops along the road. When Ming commanders Wu Sangui and Wang Pu fled from Xingshan toward Ningyuan, our forces caught them at Gaoqiao; the ambush closed and Sangui and his companions escaped only with their lives.

sentences.zh: 嗣與諸王更番圍松山，屢破敵。

translations.literal: Thereafter [he] joined the princes in taking turns besieging Songshan and repeatedly defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he and the other princes took turns investing Songshan and repeatedly broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，明松山副將夏承德遣人通款，以其子舒為質，約內應，夜半，我軍梯而登，獲承疇及巡撫邱民仰等。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year, Ming Songshan vice commander Xia Chengde sent someone to open negotiations, offered his son Shu as hostage, and agreed on an inside response; at midnight our army scaled [the walls] with ladders, captured Chengchou together with Grand Coordinator Qiu Minyang and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year the Ming vice commander at Songshan, Xia Chengde, sent envoys to treat; he gave his son Shu as hostage and arranged an inside opening. At midnight our men went up on ladders and took Chengchou, along with Grand Coordinator Qiu Minyang and others.

sentences.zh: 敘功，進豫郡王。

translations.literal: Merits were reviewed, and [he] was advanced to Prince of the Commandery of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When merits were reckoned, he was promoted to Prince of the Commandery of Yu.

sentences.zh: 复布屯寧遠邊外綴明師，俘獲甚夥。

translations.literal: Again [he] deployed garrisons outside the Ningyuan frontier to pin down Ming forces, and captures were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He again posted troops beyond the Ningyuan frontier to tie down Ming columns, and the haul of prisoners and booty was immense.

sentences.zh: 順治元年四月，從睿親王多爾袞入關，破李自成，進親王。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Shunzhi 1, [he] followed Prince Rui Dorgon in entering the pass, defeated Li Zicheng, and was advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Shunzhi 1 he followed Prince Rui Dorgon through the pass, broke Li Zicheng, and was raised to full prince.

sentences.zh: 命為定國大將軍，南征，定懷慶。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General for Settling the Realm, marched south, and pacified Huaiqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Grand General for Settling the Realm, marched south, and secured Huaiqing.

sentences.zh: 進次孟津，遣巴牙喇纛章京圖賴率兵先渡，自成守將走，沿河十五寨堡皆降。

translations.literal: Advancing, [the army] halted at Mengjin; [Dodo] dispatched Bujantai Banner Commander Tulai to lead troops across first; Zicheng's defending commander fled, and fifteen stockaded forts along the river all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The army pushed on to Mengjin. Dodo sent Bujantai Banner Commander Tulai ahead to cross the river first; Zicheng's garrison commander fled, and fifteen fortified posts along the bank surrendered.

sentences.zh: 再進次陝州，克靈寶。

translations.literal: Advancing again, [the army] halted at Shanzhou and captured Lingbao.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on, the army reached Shanzhou and took Lingbao.

sentences.zh: 再進，距潼關二十里，自成兵據山列營，噶布什賢噶喇依昂邦努山及圖賴、鄂碩等擊破之。

translations.literal: Advancing again, twenty li from Tong Pass, Zicheng's troops held the mountains and set up camps; Vanguard Commander Nushan together with Tulai, Eshuo, and others attacked and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced again to within twenty li of Tong Pass, where Zicheng's men had camped on the heights. Vanguard Commander Nushan, Tulai, Eshuo, and others drove them off.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，自成親率步騎迎戰，師奮擊，殲其步卒，騎卒奔潰。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Zicheng personally led infantry and cavalry to meet battle; the army fought fiercely, annihilated his foot soldiers, and the horsemen fled in collapse.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Zicheng came out in person with horse and foot. Our army struck hard, wiped out his infantry, and put his cavalry to rout.

sentences.zh: 及夜，屢犯屢北，鑿重壕，立堅壁。

translations.literal: By night [Zicheng] repeatedly attacked and repeatedly retreated, dug deep trenches, and raised stout ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: That night he attacked again and again, each time falling back; he dug deep trenches and threw up strong walls.

sentences.zh: 師進，發巨礮迭戰，自成兵三百騎沖我師，貝勒尼堪、貝子尚善等躍馬夾擊，屢破敵壘，屍滿壕塹，械冑彌山野，自成精銳略盡，遁歸西安，其將馬世堯率七千人降。

translations.literal: The army advanced, firing great cannon in successive battles; three hundred of Zicheng's horsemen charged our army; beile Nikan, beizi Shangshan, and others leaped on horseback and struck from both sides, repeatedly breaking enemy ramparts; corpses filled trenches and ditches, weapons and armor covered mountains and fields; Zicheng's elite were nearly exhausted; he fled back to Xi'an, and his general Ma Shiyao led seven thousand men in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Our army pressed forward, pounding the lines with heavy guns. Three hundred of Zicheng's horsemen charged in; beile Nikan, beizi Shangshan, and others spurred forward and struck from both flanks, breaking camp after camp until the ditches were choked with dead and arms and armor littered the hills. Zicheng's best troops were all but spent; he fled back to Xi'an while his general Ma Shiyao surrendered with seven thousand men.

sentences.zh: 入潼關，獲世堯所遣致自成書，斬以徇。

translations.literal: Entering Tong Pass, [they] obtained a letter Shiyao had sent to Zicheng, beheaded [the bearer] and displayed [the head] as warning.
translations.idiomatic: On entering Tong Pass they seized a letter Shiyao had sent to Zicheng; the messenger was beheaded and the head displayed as a warning.

sentences.zh: 進次西安，自成先五日毀室廬，挈子女輜重，出藍田口，竄商州，南走湖廣。

translations.literal: Advancing, [the army] halted at Xi'an; five days earlier Zicheng had destroyed houses and dwellings, taken wives, children, and baggage train, gone out through Lantian Pass, fled into Shangzhou, and marched south toward Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Xi'an to find that Zicheng, five days before, had burned his quarters, gathered up family and baggage, slipped out through Lantian Pass, fled into Shangzhou, and was already heading south into Huguang.

sentences.zh: 二月，詔以陝西賊付英親王阿濟格，趣多鐸自河南趨淮、揚。

translations.literal: In the second month, an edict assigned the Shaanxi bandits to Prince Ying Ajige and ordered Dodo to hurry from Henan toward the Huai and Yang [regions].
translations.idiomatic: In the second month an edict turned the Shaanxi rebels over to Prince Ying Ajige and ordered Dodo to press from Henan toward the Huai and Yang regions.

sentences.zh: 師退徇南陽、開封，趨歸德，諸州縣悉降。

translations.literal: The army withdrew, marched through Nanyang and Kaifeng, pressed toward Guide, and all prefectures and counties submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The army turned back, swept through Nanyang and Kaifeng, pushed on to Guide, and every prefecture and county along the way surrendered.

sentences.zh: 所至設官吏，安集流亡。

translations.literal: Wherever [they] arrived, [they] established officials and settled displaced persons.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they went they installed officials and gathered in the displaced.

sentences.zh: 詔褒多鐸功，賜嵌珠佩刀、䤹金鞓帶。

translations.literal: An edict praised Dodo's merits and granted him a pearl-inlaid girdle dagger and a gold-inlaid girdle belt.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended Dodo's service and gave him a pearl-inlaid dress dagger and a gold-inlaid girdle belt.

sentences.zh: 四月，師進次泗州，渡淮趨揚州，遣兵部尚書漢岱等先驅，得舟三百餘，圍七日，克之，殺明大學士史可法。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the army advanced and halted at Sizhou, crossed the Huai and pressed toward Yangzhou, dispatched Minister of War Handai and others as vanguard, obtained more than three hundred boats, besieged [the city] seven days, captured it, and killed Ming Grand Secretary Shi Kefa.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the army reached Sizhou, crossed the Huai, and bore down on Yangzhou. Minister of War Handai and others went ahead, gathered more than three hundred boats, and after a seven-day siege took the city and killed Ming Grand Secretary Shi Kefa.

sentences.zh: 五月，師再進，次揚子江北岸，明將鄭鴻逵等以水師守瓜洲、儀真。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the army advanced again and halted on the north bank of the Yangzi; Ming generals Zheng Hongkui and others guarded Guazhou and Yizhen with a river fleet.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the army pushed on again and camped on the north bank of the Yangzi, where Ming commanders such as Zheng Hongkui held Guazhou and Yizhen with a naval force.

sentences.zh: 師列營相持，造船二百餘，遣固山額真拜音圖將水師薄南岸，復遣梅勒額真李率泰護諸軍渡江。

translations.literal: The army set camps and faced off; [they] built more than two hundred boats, dispatched Gushan ejen Bayintu to lead the river fleet close to the south bank, and again dispatched mele ejen Li Shuaitai to escort the armies across the river.
translations.idiomatic: The armies faced each other in camp. More than two hundred boats were built; Gushan ejen Bayintu was sent with the fleet to press the south bank, and mele ejen Li Shuaitai was sent to cover the crossing.

sentences.zh: 明福王由崧走太平。

translations.literal: Ming's Prince of Fu, Zhu Yousong, fled to Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Fu, Zhu Yousong, fled to Taiping.

sentences.zh: 師再進，明忻城伯趙之龍等率文武將吏，籍馬步兵二十三萬有奇，使迎師。

translations.literal: The army advanced again; Ming's Earl of Xincheng, Zhao Zhilong, and others led civil and military officers and generals, registering more than two hundred thirty thousand cavalry and infantry, and sent [them] to welcome the army.
translations.idiomatic: The army pressed on again. Zhao Zhilong, Earl of Xincheng, and other Ming civil and military leaders mustered more than two hundred thirty thousand horse and foot and sent them out to receive our forces.

sentences.zh: 多鐸至南京，承製受其降，撫輯遺民。

translations.literal: Dodo reached Nanjing, received the imperial decree and accepted their surrender, and soothed and gathered the surviving people.
translations.idiomatic: Dodo entered Nanjing, received the imperial patent, accepted the surrender, and set about calming the people left behind.

sentences.zh: 遣貝勒尼堪、貝子屯齊徇太平，追擊明福王。

translations.literal: He dispatched beile Nikan and beizi Tunqi to march through Taiping and pursue the Ming Prince of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He sent beile Nikan and beizi Tunqi through Taiping in pursuit of the Ming Prince of Fu.

sentences.zh: 福王復走蕪湖，圖賴等邀之江口，擊殺明將黃得功，獲福王。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fu again fled to Wuhu; Tulai and others intercepted him at the river mouth, struck and killed Ming general Huang Degong, and captured the Prince of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fu fled again to Wuhu. Tulai and others cut him off at the river mouth, killed the Ming commander Huang Degong, and took the prince.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，上遣侍臣慰勞。

translations.literal: When news of victory arrived, the sovereign dispatched attendant ministers to offer consolation and reward.
translations.idiomatic: When word of the victory arrived, the emperor sent palace attendants with congratulations.

sentences.zh: 明潞王常淓守杭州，遣貝勒博洛率師討之，潞王降。

translations.literal: Ming's Prince of Lu, Zhu Changfang, held Hangzhou; [Dodo] dispatched beile Boluo to lead troops against him, and the Prince of Lu surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Lu, Zhu Changfang, held Hangzhou. Dodo sent beile Boluo against him, and the Prince of Lu submitted.

sentences.zh: 江、浙底定。

translations.literal: The Jiang and Zhe [regions] were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan and Zhejiang were brought to order.

sentences.zh: 多鐸承製改南京為江南省，疏請授江寧、安慶巡撫以下官。

translations.literal: Dodo, acting by imperial decree, changed Nanjing to Jiangnan Province and memorialized requesting appointment of officials from the Jiangning and Anqing grand coordinators downward.
translations.idiomatic: Acting by imperial mandate, Dodo renamed Nanjing as Jiangnan Province and memorialized to appoint officials down to the grand coordinators of Jiangning and Anqing.

sentences.zh: 別遣精奇尼哈番吳兆勝徇廬江、和州，並下。

translations.literal: Separately he dispatched jingkiniha Wu Zhaosheng to march through Lujiang and Hezhou; both were taken.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent jingkiniha Wu Zhaosheng to sweep Lujiang and Hezhou, and both fell.

sentences.zh: 詔遣貝勒勒克德渾代鎮江寧，召多鐸還京師。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched beile Lekedehun to replace [him] in garrisoning Jiangning and summoned Dodo back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent beile Lekedehun to take over the Jiangning garrison and recalled Dodo to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上幸南苑行郊勞禮，進封德豫親王，賜黑狐冠、紫貂朝服、金五千、銀五萬、馬十、鞍二。

translations.literal: The sovereign visited the Southern Park to perform the suburban reward ceremony, advanced [Dodo] to Virtuous Prince Yu, and granted a black-fox cap, purple-sable court robe, five thousand [taels of] gold, fifty thousand [taels of] silver, ten horses, and two saddles.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to the Southern Park for the suburban ceremony of reward, raised him to Virtuous Prince Yu, and gave him a black-fox cap, a purple-sable court robe, five thousand taels of gold, fifty thousand taels of silver, ten horses, and two saddles.

sentences.zh: 三年，命為揚威大將軍，偕承澤郡王碩塞討蘇尼特部騰機思、騰機特等。

translations.literal: In the third year, [he] was appointed Grand General for Displaying Might and, together with Prince Chenze Shuosai, campaigned against Tengjisi, Tengjite, and others of the Sonid.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was named Grand General for Displaying Might and, with Prince Chenze Shuosai, marched against Tengjisi, Tengjite, and other Sonid leaders.

sentences.zh: 師至盈阿爾察克山，聞騰機思方在袞噶嚕台，疾行三晝夜，敗之於諤特克山，斬台吉茂海。

translations.literal: The army reached Ying'erchake Mountain; hearing that Tengjisi was then at Gungarutai, [they] marched hard for three days and nights, defeated [him] at Etke Mountain, and beheaded taiji Mao Hai.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Ying'erchake Mountain. Learning that Tengjisi was at Gungarutai, they forced the march for three days and nights, routed him at Etke Mountain, and beheaded taiji Mao Hai.

sentences.zh: 渡圖拉河，追至布爾哈圖山，斬騰機特子二、騰機思孫三，盡獲其孥。

translations.literal: Crossing the Tula River, [they] pursued to Burhatu Mountain, beheaded two sons of Tengjite and three grandsons of Tengjisi, and captured all their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the Tula River and chased the fugitives to Burhatu Mountain, where they killed two of Tengjite's sons and three of Tengjisi's grandsons and took all their families captive.

sentences.zh: 師次扎濟布喇克，喀爾喀土謝圖汗遣兵二萬，碩雷車臣汗遣兵三萬，迎戰。

translations.literal: The army halted at Zhajibulake; the Khalkha Tushiyetu Khan dispatched twenty thousand troops, and the Shulei Sechen Khan dispatched thirty thousand troops to meet battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhajibulake the army was met in battle by twenty thousand men sent by the Khalkha Tushiyetu Khan and thirty thousand sent by the Shulei Sechen Khan.

sentences.zh: 我師奮擊，逐北三十餘裡，先後斬級數千，俘千餘，獲駝千九百、馬二萬一千一百、牛萬六千九百、羊十三萬五千三百有奇。

translations.literal: Our army fought fiercely, pursued the fleeing enemy more than thirty li, and in succession beheaded several thousand, captured more than a thousand, and obtained one thousand nine hundred camels, twenty-one thousand one hundred horses, sixteen thousand nine hundred cattle, and more than one hundred thirty-five thousand three hundred sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Our army struck hard and chased the broken enemy more than thirty li. Thousands were killed in the running fight, more than a thousand taken alive, and the booty included one thousand nine hundred camels, twenty-one thousand one hundred horses, sixteen thousand nine hundred cattle, and more than one hundred thirty-five thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 師還，上出安定門迎勞，加賜王鞍馬一。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the sovereign went out through Anding Gate to welcome and reward [them], and additionally granted one princely saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return the emperor came out through Anding Gate to welcome them and added one princely saddle horse to the rewards.

sentences.zh: 四年，進封為輔政叔德豫親王，賜金千、銀萬、鞍馬二，封冊增錄功勳。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, [he] was advanced to Prince Regent Uncle, Virtuous Prince Yu, granted one thousand [taels of] gold, ten thousand [taels of] silver, and two saddles and horses, and the patent of enfeoffment was augmented with a record of his merits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was raised to Prince Regent Uncle, Virtuous Prince Yu, given one thousand taels of gold, ten thousand taels of silver, and two saddle horses, and his patent of enfeoffment was expanded to record his achievements.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，以痘薨，年三十六。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year, [he] died of smallpox, aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year he died of smallpox, at the age of thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，睿親王既削爵，以同母弟追降郡王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year, after Prince Rui had been stripped of his title, [Dodo] was posthumously demoted to Prince of the Commandery as a younger brother of the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the ninth year, after Prince Rui's title had been revoked, Dodo was posthumously reduced to Prince of the Commandery as Dorgon's younger uterine brother.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，追諡。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi, a posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 10 a posthumous title was granted.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十三年正月，詔配享太廟。

translations.literal: In the first month of the forty-third year of Qianlong, an edict granted [him] sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Qianlong 43 an edict admitted him to shared sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 多鐸子八，有爵者四：多尼、董額、察尼、多爾博、費揚古。

translations.literal: Dodo had eight sons; four held titles: Duni, Dong'e, Chani, Duo'erbo, and Feiyanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Dodo had eight sons, of whom four held noble rank: Duni, Dong'e, Chani, Duo'erbo, and Feiyanggu.

sentences.zh: 費揚古自三等奉國將軍進封輔國公，坐事，奪爵。

translations.literal: Feiyanggu was advanced from third-rank Gurgu General to Fuguo Duke; for an offense he was stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: Feiyanggu rose from third-rank Gurgu General to Fuguo Duke, but after a conviction his title was taken away.

sentences.zh: 信宣和郡王多尼，多鐸第一子。

translations.literal: Prince Xuanhe of the Commandery, Duni, was Dodo's first son.
translations.idiomatic: Duni, Prince Xuanhe of the Commandery, was Dodo's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 初封郡王。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as Prince of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created Prince of the Commandery.

sentences.zh: 順治六年十月，襲豫親王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year of Shunzhi, [he] inherited the title Prince Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Shunzhi 6 he succeeded to the title of Prince Yu.

sentences.zh: 八年，改封信親王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, [his title] was changed to Prince Xin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was redesignated Prince Xin.

sentences.zh: 九年，降郡王。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, [he] was demoted to Prince of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was reduced to Prince of the Commandery.

sentences.zh: 十五年，命為安遠靖寇大將軍，偕平郡王羅科鐸等南征。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, [he] was appointed Grand General for Pacifying the Distance and Quelling Bandits and, together with Prince of the Commandery Luo Keduo and others, marched south.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was named Grand General for Pacifying the Distance and Quelling Bandits and, with Prince of the Commandery Luo Keduo and others, led a southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 師自湖南入貴州，趨安莊走明將白文選。

translations.literal: The army entered Guizhou from Hunan, pressed toward Anzhuang, and drove off Ming general Bai Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: The army entered Guizhou from Hunan, bore down on Anzhuang, and put Ming general Bai Wenxuan to flight.

sentences.zh: 十六年正月，薄雲南會城，定國、文選挾桂王走永昌，遣貝勒尚善以師從之，克永昌及騰越。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixteenth year, [they] drew close to the Yunnan provincial capital; Ding Guo and Wenxuan took the Prince of Gui and fled to Yongchang. [Duni] dispatched beile Shangshan with troops to follow them and captured Yongchang and Tengyue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixteenth year they approached the Yunnan capital. Li Dingguo and Bai Wenxuan fled with the Prince of Gui to Yongchang, and Duni sent beile Shangshan in pursuit; Yongchang and Tengyue were taken.

sentences.zh: 上使慰勞，賜禦衣、蟒袍及鞍馬、弓矢。

translations.literal: The sovereign sent envoys to console [him] and granted an imperial robe, a python robe, saddle horses, and bow and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys with words of praise and gave him an imperial robe, a python-patterned robe, saddle horses, and bow and arrows.

sentences.zh: 十七年五月，師還，遣內大臣迎勞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year, when the army returned, [the court] dispatched a grand secretary to welcome and reward [them].
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned in the fifth month of the seventeenth year, a grand secretary was sent out to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 六月，追論雲南誤坐噶布什賢昂邦瑚理布等磨盤山敗績罪，罰銀五千。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, a retrospective inquiry held [him] accountable for wrongly punishing gabushi xian angbang Hulibu and others over the defeat at Mopanshan in Yunnan; [he] was fined five thousand [taels of] silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was retrospectively fined five thousand taels of silver for having wrongly punished gabushi xian angbang Hulibu and others for the defeat at Mopanshan in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 十八年正月，薨，諡曰宣和。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighteenth year, [he] died; his posthumous title was Xuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of the eighteenth year and was posthumously titled Xuanhe.

sentences.zh: 子鄂扎，嗣。

translations.literal: His son E'zha succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son E'zha succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年，命為撫遠大將軍，討察哈爾布爾尼。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi, [he] was appointed Grand General for Pacifying the Distant Regions to campaign against the Chakhar Burni.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 14 he was named Grand General for Pacifying the Distant Regions and sent against the Chakhar leader Burni.

sentences.zh: 師次岐爾哈台，诇知布爾尼屯達祿。

translations.literal: The army halted at Qierhatai; scouts reported that Burni was encamped at Dalu.
translations.idiomatic: The army encamped at Qierhatai, where scouts learned that Burni was stationed at Dalu.

sentences.zh: 鄂扎令留輜重，偕副將軍圖海及梅勒額真吳丹輕騎進。

translations.literal: E'zha ordered the baggage train left behind and, together with deputy general Tu Hai and mele ejen Wu Dan, advanced with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: E'zha left the supply train behind and pushed forward with deputy general Tu Hai and mele ejen Wu Dan at the head of a light cavalry force.

sentences.zh: 布爾尼設伏待，命分軍搜山澗，伏發，師與土默特兵合擊破之。

translations.literal: Burni set an ambush and waited; [E'zha] ordered troops divided to search the mountains and streams. The ambush was sprung; the army joined with Tumed troops in a combined attack and broke [the enemy].
translations.idiomatic: Burni lay in ambush. E'zha sent detachments to sweep the hills and ravines, and when the trap was sprung his men joined Tumed forces in a combined assault that broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 布爾尼督兵列火器以拒，師奮擊，布爾尼大敗；

translations.literal: Burni personally led troops arrayed with fire weapons to resist; the army fought fiercely and Burni was heavily defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Burni himself drew up his men behind firearms to hold the line, but after a fierce assault he was routed.

sentences.zh: 復收潰卒再戰，又擊殲之，獲馬械無算。

translations.literal: He again gathered the scattered troops for another battle; [they] were again attacked and annihilated, and horses and weapons beyond count were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Burni rallied his broken troops for a second stand, but they were struck down again; horses and arms were taken in numbers beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 布爾尼以三十騎遁，中途為科爾沁部長沙津射死。

translations.literal: Burni fled with thirty horsemen; midway he was shot dead by Korcin chief Shajin.
translations.idiomatic: Burni escaped with thirty riders, but on the road Korcin chief Shajin shot him dead.

sentences.zh: 察哈爾平，撫餘黨一​​千三百餘戶。

translations.literal: The Chakhar were pacified, and more than one thousand three hundred remaining households were settled.
translations.idiomatic: With the Chakhar subdued, more than thirteen hundred remaining households were brought under control.

sentences.zh: 師還，上迎勞南苑，詔褒功，賜金百、銀五千。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the sovereign welcomed and rewarded [them] at the Southern Park; an edict praised their merits and granted one hundred [taels of] gold and five thousand [taels of] silver.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return the emperor received them at the Southern Park, commended their achievement in an edict, and granted one hundred taels of gold and five thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 尋掌宗人府事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward [he] took charge of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon put in charge of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，副恭親王常寧備噶爾丹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, [he] assisted Prince Gong Changning in preparing against Galdan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he served under Prince Gong Changning in preparations against Galdan.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，從上北征，領正白旗營。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, [he] followed the sovereign on the northern expedition and commanded the Plain White Banner camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year he joined the emperor's northern expedition and led the Plain White Banner division.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，以惰，解宗人府。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, for indolence, [he] was removed from the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year he was dismissed from the Court of the Imperial Clan for negligence.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，薨，以多鐸子董額襲。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, [he] died; Dong'e, son of Dodo, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-first year, and Dodo's son Dong'e succeeded.

sentences.zh: 信郡王董額，多鐸第三子。

translations.literal: Prince Xin of the Commandery, Dong'e, was Dodo's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Dong'e, Prince Xin of the Commandery, was Dodo's third son.

sentences.zh: 初封貝勒。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as a beile.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created a beile.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，命為定西大將軍，討叛將王輔臣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, [he] was appointed Grand General for Pacifying the West to campaign against rebel general Wang Fuchen.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 he was named Grand General for Pacifying the West and sent against the rebel general Wang Fuchen.

sentences.zh: 董額遣將梅勒額真赫業等守鳳翔，而率師駐西安。

translations.literal: Dong'e dispatched mele ejen He Ye and others to guard Fengxiang and personally led the army to garrison Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Dong'e left mele ejen He Ye and others to hold Fengxiang and himself encamped the main force at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 詔令進駐蘭州，董額未即行，上復命嚴守棧道。

translations.literal: An edict ordered [him] to advance and garrison Lanzhou; Dong'e did not set out at once, and the sovereign again ordered strict defense of the plank road.
translations.idiomatic: An edict told him to move up and garrison Lanzhou, but Dong'e did not march immediately, and the emperor again ordered the plank roads held firmly.

sentences.zh: 輔臣遣兵毀偏橋，斷棧道。

translations.literal: Fuchen sent troops to destroy the side bridges and cut the plank road.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchen sent men to wreck the trestle bridges and sever the plank roads.

sentences.zh: 詔責董額遷延，仍趣攻下平涼、秦州諸路。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked Dong'e for delay and still urged [him] to attack and capture the routes of Pingliang and Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict censured Dong'e for stalling but still pressed him to take Pingliang and the Qinzhou line.

sentences.zh: 董額進克秦州禮縣，逐敵至西和，克清水、伏羌。

translations.literal: Dong'e advanced, captured Li County in Qinzhou, pursued the enemy to Xihe, and captured Qingshui and Fuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Dong'e pushed forward, took Li County in Qinzhou, chased the enemy to Xihe, and captured Qingshui and Fuyao.

sentences.zh: 復遣安西將軍穆佔取鞏昌，蘭州亦下。

translations.literal: Again he dispatched Anxi General Mugan to take Gongchang, and Lanzhou also fell.
translations.idiomatic: He next sent Anxi General Mugan to seize Gongchang, and Lanzhou fell as well.

sentences.zh: 尋與將軍畢力克圖、阿密達會師攻平涼，久未下。

translations.literal: Soon afterward [he] joined generals Biligetu and Amida to besiege Pingliang, but after a long time [it] was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined generals Biligetu and Amida in the siege of Pingliang, but the city long held out.

sentences.zh: 十五年，命大學士圖海視師，改授董額固山額真，聽圖海節制。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Grand Secretary Tu Hai was ordered to inspect the army; Dong'e was changed to gushan ejen and placed under Tu Hai's command.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Grand Secretary Tu Hai was sent to take command of the campaign; Dong'e was made gushan ejen and placed under his orders.

sentences.zh: 十六年二月，削貝勒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixteenth year, [he] was stripped of beile rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixteenth year his beile title was revoked.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，授正藍旗固山額真。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, [he] was appointed gushan ejen of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was made gushan ejen of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，襲郡王。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, [he] inherited the title Prince of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year he succeeded to the title of Prince of the Commandery.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，薨。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, [he] died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-fifth year.

sentences.zh: 仍坐前罪，不賜卹。

translations.literal: He was still held accountable for his previous offense, and no funeral gifts were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Because his earlier offense still stood against him, no state funeral gifts were granted.

sentences.zh: 以鄂扎子德昭襲。

translations.literal: E'zha's son Dezhao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: E'zha's son Dezhao succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，歷左、右宗正。

translations.literal: During the Yongzheng reign, he successively held the posts of Left and Right Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng he served in turn as director of the Imperial Clan Court on both the left and the right.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十七年，薨，諡曰慤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Qianlong, [he] died; posthumous title: Earnest.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qianlong 27 (1762) and was posthumously honored with the epithet Earnest.

sentences.zh: 以多鐸五世孫如松襲。

translations.literal: Dodo's fifth-generation descendant Rusong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed to Rusong, Dodo's fifth-generation descendant.

sentences.zh: 如松四世祖多爾博，多鐸第五子。

translations.literal: Rusong's fourth-generation ancestor was Duoerbo, Dodo's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong's fourth-generation forebear was Duoerbo, the fifth son of Dodo.

sentences.zh: 初出為睿親王多爾袞後。

translations.literal: At first he was given out to succeed Prince Rui Dorgon.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally been placed in adoption to succeed Prince Rui Dorgon.

sentences.zh: 多爾袞薨後，削爵。

translations.literal: After Dorgon died, [his rank] was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: When Dorgon died, the ennoblement was revoked.

sentences.zh: 多爾博歸宗，封貝勒。

translations.literal: Duoerbo returned to his original clan and was enfeoffed as a beile.
translations.idiomatic: Duoerbo was restored to his birth line and created a beile.

sentences.zh: 多爾博生蘇爾發，襲貝子。

translations.literal: Duoerbo begot Su'erfa, who succeeded as a beizi.
translations.idiomatic: Duoerbo's son Su'erfa inherited the title of beizi.

sentences.zh: 蘇爾發生塞勒，塞勒生功宜布，皆襲輔國公。

translations.literal: Su'erfa begot Saile; Saile begot Gongyibu — all succeeded as dukes who assist the state.
translations.idiomatic: Su'erfa was followed by Saile and then Gongyibu; each in turn inherited the dukedom of the state who assists the country.

sentences.zh: 內大臣，綏遠城、西安將軍。

translations.literal: [He was] an inner minister and commander at Suiyuancheng and Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He served as an inner minister and as military commander at Suiyuancheng and Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，复授都統、右宗正。

translations.literal: [He] succeeded to the title and was again appointed banner commander and Right Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Rusong inherited the title and was again appointed banner commander and director of the Imperial Clan Court on the right.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，薨，諡曰恪。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, [he] died; posthumous title: Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year he died and received the posthumous epithet Reverent.

sentences.zh: 尋以子淳穎襲睿親王，追進封。

translations.literal: Soon afterward his son Chunying succeeded to Prince Rui, and [Rusong] was posthumously advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, his son Chunying inherited the title of Prince Rui, and Rusong was posthumously promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 具睿親王多爾袞傳。

translations.literal: The full account appears in the biography of Prince Rui Dorgon.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is given in the biography of Prince Rui Dorgon.

sentences.zh: 功宜布初薨，以德昭子修齡襲輔國公，授左宗正。

translations.literal: When Gongyibu first died, Dezhao's son Xiuling succeeded as duke who assists the state and was appointed Left Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongyibu died, Xiuling, son of Dezhao, inherited the dukedom and was appointed director of the Imperial Clan Court on the left.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，复襲豫親王。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, [he] again succeeded to Prince Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he was restored to the title of Prince Yu.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，薨，諡曰良。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year, [he] died; posthumous title: Good.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year he died and was posthumously honored with the epithet Good.

sentences.zh: 子裕豐，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yufeng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yufeng inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十八年，林清之變，所屬有從亂者，坐奪爵。
