translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jiaqing, during the Lin Qing affair, among his dependents were those who joined the rebellion; for this he was stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 18 (1813), when the Lin Qing uprising broke out, some of his household joined the rebels, and he was deprived of his title.

sentences.zh: 弟裕興，襲。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yuxing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yuxing inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，姦婢，婢自殺。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, [he] violated a maidservant, and the maidservant killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he forced himself on a maidservant, who then took her own life.

sentences.zh: 仁宗諭曰：「國家法令，王公與庶民共之。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong edicted: "The laws of the state are shared by princes and commoners alike.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong issued an edict: "The laws of the realm bind princes and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 裕興不自愛惜，恣意幹紀，且親喪未滿，國服未除，罪孰大焉！

translations.literal: Yuxing did not cherish himself, wantonly violated discipline, and moreover his mourning for a parent was not yet complete, nor had he laid aside national mourning garb — what crime could be greater!
translations.idiomatic: Yuxing has shown no regard for himself, has wantonly broken the law, and has done so while still in mourning for a parent and before laying aside court mourning dress — what offense could be more grave!

sentences.zh: 」坐奪爵，幽禁。

translations.literal: " For this he was stripped of his title and placed under house arrest.
translations.idiomatic: " He was stripped of his title and confined.

sentences.zh: 三年後釋之。

translations.literal: After three years he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was released.

sentences.zh: 弟豫全，襲。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yuquan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yuquan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 道光二十年，薨，諡曰厚。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Daoguang, [he] died; posthumous title: Generous.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Daoguang 20 (1840) and received the posthumous epithet Generous.

sentences.zh: 子義道，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yidao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yidao inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 歷內大臣、左宗正。

translations.literal: He successively served as inner minister and Left Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He served as an inner minister and as director of the Imperial Clan Court on the left.

sentences.zh: 同治七年，薨，諡曰慎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tongzhi, [he] died; posthumous title: Cautious.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tongzhi 7 (1868) and was posthumously honored with the epithet Cautious.

sentences.zh: 子本格，襲。

translations.literal: His son Benge succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Benge inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 亦歷內大臣、左宗正。

translations.literal: He also successively served as inner minister and Left Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He too served as an inner minister and as director of the Imperial Clan Court on the left.

sentences.zh: 德宗大婚，賜四團正龍補服。

translations.literal: At the Dezong Emperor's grand wedding, [he] was granted a surcoat with four roundels bearing full-front facing dragons.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong celebrated his grand wedding, he was granted the court surcoat bearing four roundels with full-front facing dragons.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十四年，薨，諡曰誠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu, [he] died; posthumous title: Sincere.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Guangxu 24 (1898) and received the posthumous epithet Sincere.

sentences.zh: 子懋林，襲。

translations.literal: His son Maolin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Maolin inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 輔國恪僖公察尼，多鐸第四子。

translations.literal: Duke of the State Who Assists the Country, posthumously Reverent and Merry, Chani — Dodo's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Chani, Duke of the State Who Assists the Country with the posthumous epithets Reverent and Merry, was Dodo's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 順治十三年，封貝勒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi, [he] was enfeoffed as a beile.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 13 (1656) he was created a beile.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，授左宗正。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi, [he] was appointed Left Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 7 (1668) he was appointed director of the Imperial Clan Court on the left.

sentences.zh: 十二年，吳三桂反，從順承郡王勒爾錦南征，參贊軍務。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Wu Sangui rebelled; [Chani] followed Prince Shuncheng Le'erjin on the southern expedition and assisted in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, when Wu Sangui rose in rebellion, he joined Prince Shuncheng Le'erjin's southern campaign as a deputy in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 師次荊州，三桂已陷岳州。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Jingzhou, Sangui had already taken Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: The army encamped at Jingzhou, by which time Sangui had already captured Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 察尼偕將軍尼雅翰舟師進，三桂將吳應麒引七萬人自陸路來拒，擊卻之。

translations.literal: Chani, together with General Niyahan's river fleet, advanced; Sangui's general Wu Yingqi led seventy thousand men by land to oppose them, and they were beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: Chani advanced with General Niyahan's fleet, and when Sangui's general Wu Yingqi brought seventy thousand men overland to block them, they drove the enemy back.

sentences.zh: 師次七里山，發礮沉其舟十餘。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Qilishan, [they] opened fire with cannon and sank more than ten of the enemy's boats.
translations.idiomatic: At Qilishan they brought up cannon and sank more than ten enemy vessels.

sentences.zh: 方暑，還駐荊州。

translations.literal: It being midsummer, [they] withdrew and encamped again at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the height of summer they withdrew and went into camp at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十四年，佩靖寇將軍印，援穀城。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, [he] wore the seal of Pacification General and went to relieve Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he bore the seal of Pacification General and marched to relieve Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 時南漳、興山已陷，敵逼彝陵，踞鎮荊山，掘壕為寨。

translations.literal: At that time Nanzhang and Xingshan had already fallen; the enemy pressed on Yiling, occupied Zhenjing Mountain, and dug trenches to make fortified camps.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhang and Xingshan had already fallen; the enemy pressed toward Yiling, held Zhenjing Mountain, and dug trenches to build fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 察尼至彝陵，議增舟師，斷餉道。

translations.literal: Chani reached Yiling, deliberated on increasing the river fleet, and cut off the supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: Chani reached Yiling, proposed reinforcing the river fleet, and severed the enemy supply lines.

sentences.zh: 擊敵牛皮丫口，進攻黃連坪，焚其積聚，取興山。

translations.literal: He struck the enemy at Niupiyakou, advanced to attack Huanglianping, burned their stores, and took Xingshan.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked the enemy at Niupiyakou, pressed the assault on Huanglianping, burned their stockpiles, and recovered Xingshan.

sentences.zh: 十五年，三桂移南漳、彝陵兵往長沙，勒爾錦令察尼還荊州，渡江趨石首，據虎渡口，擊敵太平街，斬三百餘級。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Sangui shifted the troops at Nanzhang and Yiling toward Changsha; Le'erjin ordered Chani back to Jingzhou, to cross the river and hurry to Shishou, hold Hudukou, strike the enemy at Taipingjie, and behead more than three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Sangui shifted his forces from Nanzhang and Yiling toward Changsha. Le'erjin ordered Chani back to Jingzhou to cross the river toward Shishou, seize Hudu Crossing, attack the enemy at Taipingjie, and take more than three hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 翌日再出，遇伏，敗還荊州。

translations.literal: The next day [he] went out again, encountered an ambush, was defeated, and withdrew to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he marched out again, walked into an ambush, and retreated in defeat to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔責其無能。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked him for incompetence.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict censured him for incompetence.

sentences.zh: 十七年八月，貝勒尚善薨於軍，命察尼代為安遠靖寇大將軍，規岳州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventeenth year, Beile Shangshan died in camp; Chani was ordered to replace him as Grand General for Pacifying the Distant and Quelling Rebels, with plans against Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Kangxi 17 (1678), Beile Shangshan died at the front. Chani was appointed Grand General for Pacifying the Distant and Quelling Rebels in his stead and directed operations against Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「舟師入湖，賊餉將絕。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "When the fleet enters the lake, the rebels' supplies will soon be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Once our fleet enters Dongting Lake, the rebels' supply lines will be severed.

sentences.zh: 宜於湖水涸後，圍以木栰，立椿列礮，以小舟徼巡，為久困計。

translations.literal: After the lake waters fall, we should ring them with log rafts, set piles and array cannon, and patrol with small boats—a plan for a long siege."
translations.idiomatic: When the water recedes we should encircle them with log rafts, drive piles, line up guns, and patrol with light craft—thus to wear them down over time."

sentences.zh: 」上善其言，令副都統關保濟師。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his plan and ordered Vice Commander-in-Chief Guan Bao to reinforce the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved the proposal and sent Vice Commander Guan Bao with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 尋破敵南津港，斬千級。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he routed the enemy at Nanjingang and beheaded a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He soon smashed the rebels at Nanjin Harbor and took a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 都統葉儲赫等進攻岳州，复破敵萬餘人。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Ye Chuhe and others pressed the attack on Yuezhou and again defeated more than ten thousand of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Ye Chuhe and others assaulted Yuezhou and routed another ten thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 屢疏請增調水陸軍合圍，上皆許之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized asking for more land and naval forces to complete the encirclement, and the Emperor granted each request.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked for additional land and river forces to tighten the siege, and each time the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 十八年正月，三桂將王度衝、陳珀等以舟師降，應麒棄城遁，遂復岳州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighteenth year, Sangui's generals Wang Duchong, Chen Bo, and others surrendered with the fleet; Ying Qi abandoned the city and fled, and Yuezhou was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kangxi 18, Wu Sangui's admirals Wang Duchong and Chen Bo surrendered with their fleet. Ying Qi fled the city, and Yuezhou fell back into Qing hands.

sentences.zh: 降官吏六百餘、兵五千餘，獲舟六十五、礮六百四十有奇。

translations.literal: More than six hundred officials and over five thousand soldiers surrendered; sixty-five boats and more than six hundred forty cannon were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Over six hundred officials and five thousand troops came over; the victors seized sixty-five vessels and more than six hundred forty guns.

sentences.zh: 二月，安親王岳樂自長沙進取衡州，察尼發綠旗兵濟師，尋复湘陰、安鄉。

translations.literal: In the second month, Prince An Yuele advanced from Changsha toward Hengzhou; Chani sent Green Standard troops as reinforcements and soon recovered Xiangyin and Anxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Prince An Yuele marched from Changsha on Hengzhou. Chani dispatched Green Standard reinforcements and soon retook Xiangyin and Anxiang.

sentences.zh: 四月，命自常德徵辰龍關，澧州以南諸軍聽調度。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was ordered to advance from Changde against Chenlong Pass; all armies south of Lizhou were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was told to strike Chenlong Pass from Changde, with every force south of Lizhou under his orders.

sentences.zh: 十九年三月，克辰龍關，复辰州。

translations.literal: In the third month of the nineteenth year he took Chenlong Pass and recovered Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kangxi 19 he captured Chenlong Pass and restored Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「途中霪雨泥濘，士馬須休養。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "On the march torrential rain turned the roads to mud; men and horses need rest."
translations.idiomatic: He reported that ceaseless rain had churned the roads to mud and that men and horses needed rest.

sentences.zh: 」詔暫屯沅州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to encamp temporarily at Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a halt at Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，詔以貝子彰泰率師下雲南，察尼勞苦久，率滿洲兵還京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth month an edict sent Beizi Zhangtai with an army into Yunnan; Chani, worn out by long hardship, led the Manchu troops back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Beizi Zhangtai was dispatched into Yunnan while Chani, exhausted after years in the field, brought the Manchu contingent home to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 吏議退縮罪，削爵職、籍其家、幽禁，上念克岳州功，命但削爵。

translations.literal: The ministry proposed punishment for retreating: strip rank and office, confiscate the household, and imprison him; the Emperor, mindful of his merit in taking Yuezhou, ordered only the loss of his title.
translations.idiomatic: Officials urged stripping his rank, confiscating his property, and imprisoning him for withdrawal. Remembering Yuezhou, the Emperor commuted the penalty to loss of noble rank alone.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，授奉天將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed General of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 24 he was made General of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，卒，賜祭葬視輔國公，諡恪僖。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died; funeral honors were granted equal to those of a Defender Duke of the State, and he was given the posthumous title Kexi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 27. The court granted obsequies befitting a Defender Duke of the State and gave him the posthumous name Kexi (Respectful and Joyful).

sentences.zh: 費揚果，太祖第十六子。

translations.literal: Feiyanggu was the sixteenth son of the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Feiyanggu was Taizu's sixteenth son.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，坐罪賜死，削宗籍。

translations.literal: In the Taizong reign he was condemned to death by imperial gift and struck from the imperial clan register.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hong Taiji he was sentenced to death and removed from the clan rolls.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十二年，聖祖命莽古爾德格類子孫復宗籍。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year of Kangxi the Sage Ancestor ordered the descendants of Manggu'ertai and Degui restored to the clan register.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 52 the Kangxi Emperor ordered the lines of Manggu'ertai and Degui readmitted to the clan.

sentences.zh: 費揚果曾孫三等侍衛尼雅罕呈宗人府，請復宗籍。

translations.literal: Feiyanggu's great-grandson, third-rank bodyguard Niyahan, submitted a petition to the Court of the Imperial Clan asking restoration to the register.
translations.idiomatic: Feiyanggu's great-grandson Niyahan, a third-rank guardsman, petitioned the Imperial Clan Court to restore his line.

sentences.zh: 宗人府以聞，聖祖曰：「此事朕知之，但不詳耳。

translations.literal: The court reported upward; the Sage Ancestor said: "I know of this matter, but not in detail.
translations.idiomatic: When the clan court forwarded the request, the Emperor said, "I have heard of this, though not the particulars.

sentences.zh: 費揚果，太祖子，太宗時因獲大罪誅死者。

translations.literal: Feiyanggu was a son of the Taizu who, in the Taizong reign, was put to death for a grave crime."
translations.idiomatic: Feiyanggu was a son of Taizu whom Hong Taiji executed for a capital offense."

sentences.zh: 」命復宗籍，賜紅帶。

translations.literal: He ordered restoration to the clan register and granted the red belt.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the clan status restored and bestowed the red belt of nobility.
